source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And he went out from there, and comes into the hometown of him, and follow him the disciples of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out from there and comes into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus left that place and went to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus left there and went back to Nazareth, the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} grew up. His followers went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi đó và đến quê hương {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu rời khỏi nơi đó và về quê hương {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, có các môn đồ cùng đi theo.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu rời nơi đó và trở về Na-xa-rét, thị trấn nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lớn lên. Các môn đồ cùng đi với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 거기서 떠나 그분의 고향으로 오신다. 그리고 그분의 제자들이 그분을 따른다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그곳을 떠나 고향으로 가셨다. 제자들도 예수와 함께 갔다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그곳을 떠나 자라나신 마을인 나사렛으로 돌아가셨다. 제자들도 예수와 함께 갔다.

es.L: Y salió de allí, y viene a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguen {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.
es.B: Jesús se fue de allí y llegó a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos fueron con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús se fue de allí y volvió a Nazaret, el pueblo donde se había criado. Sus discípulos fueron con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit de là, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} patrie, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivent.
fr.B: Jésus partit de là et se rendit dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} ville d’origine ; {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accompagnaient.
fr.R: Jésus a quitté cet endroit et il est retourné à Nazareth, la ville où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait grandi. Ses disciples sont venus avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Naye akatoka huko, na anakuja katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa nyumbani, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wanamfuata.
sw.B: Yesu aliondoka mahali pale, akaenda katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa nyumbani, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaenda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Yesu aliondoka pale, akarudi Nazareti, mji alimokulia. Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikwenda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: hometown: Nazareth, where Jesus grew up
decisions.reason: The word means one's native place. Mark has named Nazareth as Jesus' home town (1:9, 1:24), and the synagogue scene that follows fits a small town.

decisions.choice: comes, follow: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: he came, and they followed.

decisions.choice: from there: from the house of Jairus by the lake (5:21-43)
decisions.reason: The last place named is the lakeshore town where Jairus' daughter was raised.

decisions.choice: Nazareth, the town where he grew up
decisions.reason: Readable names the town so that new readers know where Jesus went.

decisions.choice: "đến", "đi theo", "nói" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present ("comes", "follow", 6:1; "says", 6:31, 6:37-38, 6:48, 6:50). Vietnamese verbs have no tense, so Literal keeps the vividness by leaving out "đã"; Balanced and Readable narrate plainly. As in the Vietnamese John.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("오신다", "따른다", "말씀하신다"), through chapter 6
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (6:1, 6:7, 6:30-31, 6:37-38, 6:48, 6:50); Balanced and Readable use the past. Recorded once for the chapter, as in the Korean Mark 3-5.

decisions.choice: "자라나신 마을인 나사렛" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the hometown, as the English Readable does; "나사렛" is the established Protestant form.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John: Literal keeps Mark's storytelling present ("viene", "siguen"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "discípulos", as the Spanish of John does at every level, where the English Readable says "followers". This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B) and the passé composé (R); Literal uses the passé simple too but keeps Mark’s present tense where he tells a past event in the present ("il vient", "ils suivent", 6:1, 30, 31, 37-38, 45, 48); the imperfect at every level for what was going on or kept happening
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for Mark 6. The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Mark’s historic present is kept only at Literal, as in the English and as in the French John. Every pronoun for Jesus takes the deity_pronoun setting, the object pronouns and possessives French needs included; one at the start of a sentence is written plainly. Readable keeps "disciples" where the English Readable says "followers", as the French style guide asks.

decisions.choice: sa patrie (L); sa ville d’origine (B); Nazareth, la ville où il avait grandi (R)
decisions.reason: The word means his home town, Nazareth (meaning decision m1). "Patrie" is the old and literal word, also used in the saying of 6:4; Balanced says "sa ville d’origine" rather than "sa ville natale", since Jesus was not born there; Readable names the town, as the English does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anakuja, wanamfuata); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the Swahili of John and Mark 5: Literal keeps the Greek present of past events, and Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past. Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb, so the deity_pronoun spans in this chapter stand only on free pronouns and possessives ("wake", "yake", "naye", "kwake").

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every separate pronoun for Jesus
decisions.reason: The rule for Mark set at 1:2: every pronoun Spanish writes for Jesus as a separate word (él, lo, le, su, sus, mí, mi, te, tu) carries the span; a pronoun at the start of a sentence, one joined to the end of a verb, and "conmigo", "contigo", "consigo" are written plain. This applies throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ· καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα, καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ γινόμεναι;

records.literal_gloss: And having come [the] Sabbath he began to teach in the synagogue; and the many hearing were astonished, saying, From where to this [man] these things, and what the wisdom the [one] having been given to this [man], and the miracles such through the hands of him coming about?

en.L: And when the Sabbath came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach in the synagogue; and the many who heard were astonished, saying, "Where [did] this [man get] these things, and what [is] the wisdom given to this [man], and such works of power coming about through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands?"
en.B: When the Sabbath came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began teaching in the synagogue, and most of those who heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were struck with amazement. "Where did this man get all this?" they said. "What is this wisdom that has been given to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? And what are these mighty works that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands are doing?"
en.R: On the Sabbath day Jesus began to teach in the synagogue. Many people heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were amazed. They said, "Where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} learn all this? Who gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} such wisdom? How can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do these powerful miracles with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands?"

vi.L: Và khi đến ngày Sa-bát, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu giảng dạy trong nhà hội; và phần đông người nghe thì kinh ngạc, nói rằng: "Người này được những điều ấy từ đâu, và sự khôn ngoan đã ban cho người này là gì, và những việc quyền năng như thế được làm ra bởi tay ông ta?"
vi.B: Đến ngày Sa-bát, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu giảng dạy trong nhà hội. Phần đông người nghe đều sửng sốt. Họ nói: "Ông ta lấy đâu ra những điều này? Sự khôn ngoan ông ta được ban cho là thế nào? Còn những việc quyền năng do tay ông ta làm ra là sao?"
vi.R: Vào ngày Sa-bát, Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu giảng dạy trong nhà hội. Nhiều người nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và rất kinh ngạc. Họ nói: "Ông ta học ở đâu mà biết những điều này? Ai đã ban cho ông ta sự khôn ngoan như vậy? Sao ông ta có thể dùng tay mình làm những phép lạ đầy quyền năng như thế?"

ko.L: 그리고 안식일이 되자 그분이 회당에서 가르치기 시작하셨다. 그러자 듣고 있던 많은 사람이 놀라며 말했다. "이 사람이 이런 것들을 어디서 [얻었느냐]? 이 사람이 받은 지혜는 무엇이며, 그의 손으로 일어나는 이런 능력 있는 일들은 [무엇이냐]?"
ko.B: 안식일이 되자 예수께서 회당에서 가르치기 시작하셨다. 그러자 예수의 말씀을 들은 사람들 대부분이 크게 놀라며 말했다. "이 사람이 이 모든 것을 어디서 얻었을까? 이 사람이 받은 이 지혜는 대체 무엇인가? 그의 손으로 일어나는 이 능력 있는 일들은 또 무엇인가?"
ko.R: 안식일에 예수께서 회당에서 가르치기 시작하셨다. 많은 사람이 예수의 말씀을 듣고 깜짝 놀랐다. 그들이 말했다. "이 사람이 이런 것을 어디서 배웠을까? 누가 이 사람에게 이런 지혜를 주었을까? 이 사람은 어떻게 자기 손으로 이런 놀라운 일들을 할 수 있을까?"

es.L: Y llegado el sábado, comenzó a enseñar en la sinagoga; y los muchos que [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] oían se asombraban, diciendo: «¿De dónde [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vienen] a este estas cosas, y qué [es] la sabiduría que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ha sido dada a este, y tales obras de poder que se realizan por {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} manos?».
es.B: Cuando llegó el sábado, comenzó a enseñar en la sinagoga, y la mayoría de los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oían se quedaban asombrados. «¿De dónde sacó este hombre todo esto?», decían. «¿Qué sabiduría es esta que se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ha dado? ¿Y qué son estas obras poderosas que hacen {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} manos?».
es.R: El sábado, Jesús comenzó a enseñar en la sinagoga. Mucha gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escuchaba y se asombraba. Decían: «¿Dónde aprendió todo esto? ¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio tanta sabiduría? ¿Cómo puede hacer estos milagros tan poderosos con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} manos?».

fr.L: Et le sabbat venu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à enseigner dans la synagogue ; et la plupart, en [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]entendant, étaient frappés d’étonnement et disaient : « D’où [viennent] à celui-ci ces choses ? Et quelle [est] la sagesse qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a été donnée, et de tels actes de puissance qui se font par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains ? »
fr.B: Le jour du sabbat, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à enseigner dans la synagogue, et la plupart de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écoutaient étaient stupéfaits. « D’où {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} vient tout cela ? disaient-ils. Quelle est cette sagesse qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a été donnée ? Et ces miracles qui s’accomplissent par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains ? »
fr.R: Le jour du sabbat, Jésus a commencé à enseigner dans la synagogue. Beaucoup de gens {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont entendu, et ils étaient très étonnés. Ils disaient : « Où est-ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a appris tout ça ? Qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donné une telle sagesse ? Comment peut-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faire ces grands miracles avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains ? »

sw.L: Na Sabato ilipofika, alianza kufundisha katika sinagogi; na wengi waliomsikia walishangaa, wakisema, "[Mtu] huyu amepata wapi mambo haya, na ni hekima gani hii aliyopewa [mtu] huyu, na matendo ya nguvu kama haya yanayotendeka kwa mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}?"
sw.B: Sabato ilipofika, alianza kufundisha katika sinagogi, na wengi waliomsikia walishangaa sana. Wakasema, "Mtu huyu amepata wapi mambo haya yote? Ni hekima gani hii aliyopewa? Na matendo haya makuu yanayofanywa kwa mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ni ya namna gani?"
sw.R: Siku ya Sabato Yesu alianza kufundisha katika sinagogi. Watu wengi walimsikia, wakashangaa. Wakasema, "Amejifunza wapi mambo haya yote? Ni nani aliyempa hekima hii? Anawezaje kufanya miujiza hii yenye nguvu kwa mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}?"

decisions.choice: astonished: struck with amazement, not yet trust
decisions.reason: The same word as at 1:22. Here amazement turns into offense (6:3).

decisions.choice: the many: most of those present
decisions.reason: With the article the phrase means the majority of the hearers.

decisions.choice: works of power: miracles that show God's power
decisions.reason: The word means powers or mighty deeds. Mark uses it for Jesus' miracles (6:5, 6:14).

decisions.choice: given to this man: the people half admit that his wisdom is a gift from outside himself
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed. The townspeople ask where it came from because they know his family (6:3).

decisions.choice: mighty works (B); powerful miracles (R)
decisions.reason: The word joins the idea of power with the deeds it produces.

decisions.choice: "người này", "ông ta" in the townspeople's words, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The people of his hometown are astonished but not yet trusting, and soon take offense (meaning decisions). The style guide has such speakers call Jesus "người này" or "ông ta"; these are not words of reverence and take no deity_pronoun span, where the English "him" has one.

decisions.choice: "phép lạ đầy quyền năng" (R); "việc quyền năng" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Mark's word is "powers", works of power (meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep "quyền năng"; Readable says "phép lạ" (miracle), the plain word, as the English Readable does. "Dấu lạ" is kept for John's different word "sign".

decisions.choice: The townspeople speak of Jesus as "이 사람" and "그", with no honorific
decisions.reason: They are astonished but about to take offense (6:3); honorifics in their mouths would misrepresent them. The narrator still honours him, as in the Korean Mark 3:21-22.

decisions.choice: "능력 있는 일들" (L, B); "놀라운 일들" (R) for dynameis
decisions.reason: "능력" keeps the word Mark uses for power (5:30; 6:14). "기적" is avoided, since the Korean John keeps "표적" apart from it; Readable says the works were astonishing.

decisions.choice: obras de poder (L); obras poderosas (B); milagros poderosos (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "powers", deeds that show God's power (meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep the idea of power; Readable says "milagros", as the English says "miracles".

decisions.choice: actes de puissance (L); miracles (B); grands miracles (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "powers", deeds that show God’s power (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the idea of power; Balanced and Readable use "miracles", the common French word, as in 6:5 and 6:14.

decisions.choice: matendo ya nguvu (L); matendo makuu (B); miujiza yenye nguvu (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "powers": Literal says "matendo ya nguvu" (works of power) and Balanced "matendo makuu" (mighty works). Only Readable says "miujiza" (miracles), as the English Readable does; "ishara" stays reserved for the different Greek word "sign".

source.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος;

records.literal_gloss: Not this is the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon?

en.L: Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon?
en.B: Is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and a brother of James, Joses, Judas and Simon?
en.R: He is just the carpenter, is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not? He is Mary's son. His brothers are James, Joses, Judas and Simon.

vi.L: Người này chẳng phải là người thợ mộc, con trai của Ma-ri, và anh em của Gia-cơ, Giô-sê, Giu-đa và Si-môn sao?
vi.B: Ông ta chẳng phải là anh thợ mộc, con bà Ma-ri, anh em của Gia-cơ, Giô-sê, Giu-đa và Si-môn sao?
vi.R: Ông ta chỉ là anh thợ mộc thôi mà! Ông ta là con trai bà Ma-ri. Các anh em của ông ta là Gia-cơ, Giô-sê, Giu-đa và Si-môn.

ko.L: 이 사람은 그 목수, 마리아의 아들이고 야고보와 요세와 유다와 시몬의 형제가 아니냐?
ko.B: 이 사람은 그 목수가 아니냐? 마리아의 아들이고, 야고보와 요세와 유다와 시몬의 형제가 아니냐?
ko.R: 이 사람은 그냥 목수가 아니냐? 마리아의 아들이 아니냐? 이 사람의 형제들은 야고보와 요세와 유다와 시몬이 아니냐?

es.L: ¿No es este el carpintero, el hijo de María y hermano de Santiago y de Joses y de Judas y de Simón?
es.B: ¿No es este el carpintero, el hijo de María, hermano de Santiago, Joses, Judas y Simón?
es.R: No es más que el carpintero, ¿verdad? Es el hijo de María. Sus hermanos son Santiago, Joses, Judas y Simón.

fr.L: Celui-ci n’est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas le charpentier, le fils de Marie et le frère de Jacques et de Joses et de Jude et de Simon ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas le charpentier, le fils de Marie, le frère de Jacques, de Joses, de Jude et de Simon ?
fr.R: Ce n’est qu’un charpentier, non ? C’est le fils de Marie. Ses frères s’appellent Jacques, Joses, Jude et Simon.

sw.L: Je, huyu si yule seremala, mwana wa Mariamu, na ndugu wa Yakobo na Yose na Yuda na Simoni?
sw.B: Je, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} si yule seremala, mwana wa Mariamu, na ndugu wa Yakobo, Yose, Yuda na Simoni?
sw.R: Huyu ni seremala tu, sivyo? Ni mwana wa Mariamu. Ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} ni Yakobo, Yose, Yuda na Simoni.

decisions.choice: the carpenter, the son of Mary: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the son of the carpenter and of Mary
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "the son of the carpenter", which matches Matthew 13:55. Scribes may have changed it so that Jesus himself was not called a craftsman. The SBLGNT follows the great majority of manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Joses, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read Joseph, as in Matthew 13:55. Joses is a short form of the same name. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: carpenter: a builder or craftsman in wood or stone
decisions.reason: The word covers anyone who builds, in wood most often but also in stone. The point is that he is a working man they know.

decisions.choice: son of Mary: unusual, since a man was normally named by his father
alternatives: the ordinary way to name him
decisions.reason: Joseph is not mentioned. He may have died by this time, or the words may carry a slight on Jesus' birth. Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: brother: the ordinary word for a brother in the same family
alternatives: a son of Joseph by an earlier marriage
decisions.reason: The word normally means a brother. Some Christian traditions understand these men as cousins or as Joseph's sons by an earlier marriage. The text names them brothers and does not settle the question.

decisions.choice: just the carpenter, is he not?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes and is meant to belittle. Readable makes the tone plain with "just".

decisions.choice: "anh em"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese names a brother as older or younger. The Greek does not say, so the general "anh em" is used, as in the Vietnamese John (2:12; 7:3-10).

decisions.choice: "thợ mộc"
decisions.reason: The word means a builder or craftsman in wood or stone (meaning decision). "Thợ mộc" (carpenter) is the familiar word and covers the main sense; the wider sense is left to the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "목수"; Protestant name forms "마리아", "야고보", "요세", "유다", "시몬"; "형제" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "목수" is the ordinary word for a builder in wood (meaning decision). "요세" is the Protestant form of Joses, which the SBLGNT reads (meaning decision). As in the Korean Mark 3:31, "형제" does not decide whether they were younger brothers.

decisions.choice: Santiago; Joses
decisions.reason: "Santiago" is the usual Spanish name for the men called James, as in the Spanish of Galatians and James. Joses is a Greek form of Joseph; every level keeps "Joses", as at 15:40 and 15:47, so that he is not confused with Joseph.

decisions.choice: Joses; Jude
decisions.reason: Joses is kept in the form of the Greek (meaning decision m2). For this brother of Jesus French tradition says "Jude" (the name given to the letter of Jude), which also keeps him apart from Judas Iscariot; the English says "Judas". Both are proper names, and a native reviewer may prefer another form of the first.

decisions.choice: le charpentier
decisions.reason: The word covers a builder or craftsman in wood or stone (meaning decision m3); "charpentier" is the traditional French word and names a builder in wood, close to the English "carpenter".

decisions.choice: ndugu
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" is the ordinary Swahili word for a brother, but it is also used for a cousin or any kinsman, so it does not by itself say "a brother in the same family" as the meaning note does. "Kaka" is narrower but often means an older brother. A native reviewer should judge which reads more naturally here.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: And not are the sisters of him here with us?

en.L: And are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters not here with us?
en.B: And are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters not here among us?
en.R: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters live here in our town, do they not?

vi.L: Và các chị em gái của ông ta chẳng phải ở đây với chúng ta sao?
vi.B: Các chị em gái của ông ta chẳng phải đang ở đây với chúng ta sao?
vi.R: Các chị em gái của ông ta cũng đang sống trong thị trấn này với chúng ta mà!

ko.L: 그리고 그의 누이들도 여기 우리와 함께 있지 않으냐?
ko.B: 그의 누이들도 여기서 우리와 함께 살고 있지 않으냐?
ko.R: 그의 누이들도 우리 마을에 살고 있지 않으냐?

es.L: ¿Y no están {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanas aquí con nosotros?
es.B: ¿Y no viven {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanas aquí entre nosotros?
es.R: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanas viven aquí en nuestro pueblo, ¿no es cierto?

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sœurs ne sont-elles pas ici chez nous ?
fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sœurs ne sont-elles pas ici, parmi nous ?
fr.R: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sœurs habitent ici, dans notre ville, n’est-ce pas ?

sw.L: Na je, dada {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} hawako hapa pamoja nasi?
sw.B: Na je, dada {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} hawaishi hapa kati yetu?
sw.R: Na dada {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wanaishi hapa katika mji wetu, sivyo?

decisions.choice: his sisters: unnamed, but living in the town
decisions.reason: Mark names the brothers but not the sisters. They still live in Nazareth, among the people speaking.

decisions.choice: here with us: living among us
decisions.reason: The point is that the family is ordinary and well known in the town.

decisions.choice: live here in our town
decisions.reason: Readable says what "here with us" means.

source.text: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And they were taking offense at him.

en.L: And they took offense at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: And they were offended by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: So they were upset with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and would not accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và họ vấp ngã vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Thế là họ khó chịu và khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Vì vậy, họ bực bội với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và không chịu tin nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분에게 걸려 넘어지고 있었다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 예수를 못마땅하게 여겼다.
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 예수를 언짢게 여기고 받아들이지 않았다.

es.L: Y se escandalizaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Y se sentían ofendidos por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Por eso se molestaron con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} quisieron aceptar.

fr.L: Et ils se scandalisaient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Et ils étaient choqués à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet.
fr.R: Alors ils étaient fâchés contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et ne voulaient pas {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accepter.

sw.L: Nao wakakwazwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Wakachukizwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo walimkasirikia, wakakataa kumpokea.

decisions.choice: took offense: stumbled over him, so as to reject him
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip over something. They could not get past his ordinary family and so turned away from him (4:17, 14:27).

decisions.choice: were upset with him and would not accept him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that taking offense here means rejecting him.

decisions.choice: "vấp ngã vì" (L); "khó chịu và khước từ" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures stumbling over him so as to reject him (meaning decision). Literal keeps the picture; Balanced says both the offense and the rejection in plain words, since "vấp phạm" is church jargon most readers would not understand here.

decisions.choice: "걸려 넘어지다" (L); "못마땅하게 여기다" (B); "언짢게 여기고 받아들이지 않다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of stumbling, as the Korean Mark 4:17 does for this verb; Balanced and Readable say that they took offense and rejected him (meaning decision). "실족하다" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: se escandalizaban (L); se sentían ofendidos (B)
decisions.reason: "Escandalizarse de" is the Spanish verb built on the Greek one and still means taking offense so as to reject (meaning decision); Balanced uses the plainer "sentirse ofendidos".

decisions.choice: se scandaliser de (L); être choqué (B)
alternatives: il était pour eux une occasion de chute
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional French word, which comes from the Greek one; its modern sense, "to be outraged", is weaker than stumbling so as to reject him (meaning decision m1). Balanced says plainly that he offended them; Readable adds the refusal, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wakakwazwa (L); wakachukizwa (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of stumbling with "kukwazwa" (to be made to stumble, to be offended); Balanced says plainly that they were offended.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And was saying to them Jesus, Not is a prophet without honor except in the hometown of him and among the relatives of him and in the household of him.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and among his relatives and in his household."
en.B: Jesus told them, "Everywhere a prophet is honored, except in his own town, among his own kin, and in his own family."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "People everywhere honor a prophet, but not in the town where he grew up. Even his relatives and his own family do not honor him."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Một nhà tiên tri không phải là không được tôn trọng, ngoại trừ ở quê hương mình, giữa bà con mình và trong nhà mình."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Nhà tiên tri được tôn trọng ở khắp nơi, trừ ra ở quê nhà, giữa họ hàng và trong gia đình mình."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ở đâu người ta cũng tôn trọng một nhà tiên tri, trừ ở nơi người ấy lớn lên. Ngay cả họ hàng và gia đình người ấy cũng không tôn trọng người ấy."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "예언자는 자기 고향과 자기 친척들 가운데와 자기 집이 아니고서는 존경을 받지 못하는 일이 없다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "예언자는 어디서나 존경을 받는다. 다만 자기 고향과 친척들과 가족에게서만은 존경을 받지 못한다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "사람들은 어디서나 예언자를 존경한다. 그러나 예언자가 자라난 고향에서는 그렇지 않다. 그의 친척들과 가족마저 그를 존경하지 않는다."

es.L: Y Jesús les decía: «No hay profeta sin honra sino en su tierra, y entre sus parientes, y en su casa».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «En todas partes se honra a un profeta, menos en su propio pueblo, entre sus parientes y en su propia familia».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «La gente en todas partes honra a un profeta, pero no en el pueblo donde se crio. Ni siquiera sus parientes y su propia familia lo honran».

fr.L: Et Jésus leur disait : « Un prophète n’est sans honneur que dans sa patrie, parmi sa parenté et dans sa maison. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Partout on honore un prophète, sauf dans sa propre ville, parmi ses proches et dans sa propre famille. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Partout, les gens respectent un prophète, mais pas dans la ville où il a grandi. Même ses proches et sa propre famille ne le respectent pas. »

sw.L: Na Yesu alikuwa akiwaambia, "Nabii hayuko bila heshima, isipokuwa katika mji wake wa nyumbani, na kati ya ndugu zake, na katika nyumba yake."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Nabii huheshimiwa kila mahali, isipokuwa katika mji wake mwenyewe, kati ya jamaa zake, na katika familia yake."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Watu kila mahali humheshimu nabii, lakini si katika mji alimokulia. Hata jamaa zake na familia yake mwenyewe hawamheshimu."

decisions.choice: a saying about prophets that Jesus applies to himself
decisions.reason: The words have the form of a proverb. By using it here, Jesus counts himself a prophet rejected by his own.

decisions.choice: household: his own family
decisions.reason: The list narrows from town to relatives to his own family, as in 3:21 and 3:31.

decisions.choice: said: an imperfect, he was saying
decisions.reason: Mark often uses this form for Jesus' sayings. It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: everywhere a prophet is honored, except (B); people everywhere honor a prophet, but not (R)
alternatives: a prophet is not without honor except
decisions.reason: The double negative is turned into a positive statement, which says the same thing more plainly.

decisions.choice: sa parenté (L); ses proches (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "ses parents" would first mean his father and mother; the word means his relatives, so Literal says "sa parenté" and Balanced and Readable "ses proches".

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν, εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν·

records.literal_gloss: And not he was able there to do not any work of power, except on a few sick having laid the hands he healed;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not able to do any work of power there, except that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on a few sick [people and] healed [them];
en.B: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not able to do any mighty work, apart from laying {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on a few who were sick and healing them.
en.R: Jesus was not able to do any powerful miracles there. The only thing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did was to heal a few sick people by putting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không thể làm một việc quyền năng nào ở đó, ngoại trừ đặt tay trên một ít người bệnh mà chữa lành;
vi.B: Ở đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không thể làm việc quyền năng nào, ngoài việc đặt tay chữa lành một vài người bệnh.
vi.R: Ở đó Đức Giê-xu không thể làm phép lạ nào. Ngài chỉ đặt tay trên một vài người bệnh và chữa lành họ thôi.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 거기서 능력 있는 일을 하나도 하실 수 없었다. 다만 병자 몇 사람에게 손을 얹어 고쳐 주셨을 뿐이다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 거기서 능력 있는 일을 하나도 하실 수 없었다. 몇몇 병자에게 손을 얹어 고쳐 주셨을 뿐이다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 거기서 놀라운 일을 하나도 하실 수 없었다. 몇몇 아픈 사람들에게 손을 얹어 고쳐 주신 것이 전부였다.

es.L: Y no podía hacer allí ninguna obra de poder, salvo que sanó a unos pocos enfermos imponiéndoles las manos;
es.B: Allí no pudo hacer ninguna obra poderosa, aparte de poner las manos sobre unos pocos enfermos y sanarlos.
es.R: Jesús no pudo hacer allí ningún milagro poderoso. Lo único que hizo fue sanar a unos pocos enfermos poniendo las manos sobre ellos.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne pouvait faire là aucun acte de puissance, sinon qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} imposa les mains à quelques malades [et les] guérit ;
fr.B: Il ne put faire là aucun miracle, si ce n’est qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} posa les mains sur quelques malades et les guérit.
fr.R: Jésus n’a pas pu faire de grands miracles là-bas. La seule chose qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faite, c’est guérir quelques malades en posant les mains sur eux.

sw.L: Wala hakuweza kufanya huko tendo lolote la nguvu, isipokuwa aliweka mikono [{{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}] juu ya wagonjwa wachache, akawaponya;
sw.B: Huko hakuweza kufanya tendo lolote kuu, isipokuwa kuweka mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu ya wagonjwa wachache na kuwaponya.
sw.R: Yesu hakuweza kufanya miujiza yenye nguvu huko. Alichoweza kufanya ni kuwaponya wagonjwa wachache tu kwa kuweka mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yao.

decisions.choice: not able: Mark links this with their unbelief (6:6)
decisions.reason: Mark says plainly that Jesus could not. In Mark, miracles answer faith (5:34). Where people would not trust him, they did not come to him, and his deeds would not have been signs to them. Mark does not explain further.

decisions.choice: laid his hands on: a touch to heal
decisions.reason: Jesus heals by touch elsewhere too (1:41; 5:23).

decisions.choice: except: the few healings are a small exception
decisions.reason: Even healing a few people is not counted as a work of power here, so few were they.

source.text: καὶ ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was marveling because of the unbelief of them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was amazed because of their unbelief.
en.B: Their unbelief amazed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was amazed that they did not believe.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngạc nhiên vì sự vô tín của họ.
vi.B: Ngài ngạc nhiên vì lòng vô tín của họ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu ngạc nhiên vì họ không tin.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들의 불신 때문에 놀라셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 그들이 믿지 않는 것을 이상히 여기셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 그들이 믿지 않는 것을 보고 놀라셨다.

es.L: Y se maravillaba por la incredulidad de ellos.
es.B: Su incredulidad {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejó asombrado.
es.R: Jesús estaba asombrado de que no creyeran.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’étonnait de leur incrédulité.
fr.B: Leur incrédulité {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}étonnait.
fr.R: Jésus était très étonné qu’ils ne croient pas.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akistaajabu kwa sababu ya kutoamini kwao.
sw.B: Kutoamini kwao kulimshangaza.
sw.R: Yesu alishangaa kwamba hawakuamini.

decisions.choice: unbelief: refusal to trust
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of faith. It is set against the faith of the woman and of Jairus (5:34, 5:36).

decisions.choice: he was amazed: Jesus himself marvels
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Mark the people marvel at Jesus. Here he marvels at them.

decisions.choice: "불신" (L); "믿지 않는 것" (B, R) for apistia
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun; Balanced and Readable use the verb "믿다", which keeps the link with "믿음" (5:34) and "믿다" (5:36).

decisions.choice: kutoamini
decisions.reason: The verbal noun "kutoamini" (not believing) keeps the link with "kuamini" (believe, 5:36) that the Greek has.

source.text: Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων.

records.literal_gloss: And he was going around the villages in a circle teaching.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going around the villages in a circuit, teaching.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went from village to village in that area, teaching.
en.R: Then Jesus went to the villages all around and taught the people there.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi khắp các làng chung quanh mà giảng dạy.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi từ làng này sang làng khác trong vùng ấy để giảng dạy.
vi.R: Sau đó Đức Giê-xu đi đến các làng chung quanh và dạy dỗ dân chúng ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 두루 마을들을 돌아다니시며 가르치고 계셨다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 예수께서는 그 일대의 마을들을 두루 다니시며 가르치셨다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서는 주변 마을들을 다니시며 사람들을 가르치셨다.

es.L: Y recorría las aldeas de alrededor enseñando.
es.B: Después iba de aldea en aldea por aquella región, enseñando.
es.R: Después Jesús fue a las aldeas de los alrededores y enseñaba a la gente.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parcourait les villages à la ronde, en enseignant.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} alla de village en village dans les environs, pour enseigner.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus est allé dans les villages tout autour et y a enseigné les gens.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akizunguka katika vijiji kandokando, akifundisha.
sw.B: Kisha akapita kijiji kwa kijiji katika eneo lile, akifundisha.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alikwenda katika vijiji vyote vya kandokando, akawafundisha watu huko.

decisions.choice: he was going around teaching: a tour that went on for some time
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense and the participle describe ongoing work.

decisions.choice: in a circle: in the area around
decisions.reason: The word means round about. He visited the villages near Nazareth.

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο, καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων, καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον, μὴ ἄρτον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν, ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια, καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας.

records.literal_gloss: And he calls to [him] the twelve, and began them to send out two [by] two, and was giving them authority over the spirits the unclean; \v 8 and he instructed them that nothing they should take for [the] road except a staff only, not bread, not bag, not in the belt copper, \v 9 but having been shod with sandals, and do not put on two tunics.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls the twelve to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and began to send them out two by two, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority over the unclean spirits; \v 8 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructed them to take nothing for the road except a staff only: no bread, no bag, no copper [money] in the belt, \v 9 but to wear sandals; and "Do not put on two tunics."
en.B: He called the Twelve to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and began sending them out in pairs, giving them authority over unclean spirits. \v 8 He told them to take nothing for the journey except a walking stick: no food, no traveler's bag, and no coins in their belts. \v 9 They were to wear sandals. "And do not put on a second tunic," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.
en.R: Jesus called the Twelve together. He began to send them out two at a time, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them power over evil spirits. \v 8 He told them, "Take nothing with you for the trip except a walking stick. Do not take any food or a bag or any money. \v 9 Wear sandals, but do not take extra clothes."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi mười hai [người] đến, và bắt đầu sai họ đi từng đôi một, và ban cho họ quyền trên các linh ô uế; \v 8 và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} truyền cho họ đừng mang gì theo dọc đường ngoại trừ một cây gậy mà thôi: không bánh, không bao bị, không tiền đồng trong thắt lưng, \v 9 nhưng [hãy] mang dép, và: "Đừng mặc hai áo."
vi.B: Ngài gọi nhóm Mười Hai đến và bắt đầu sai họ đi từng đôi, ban cho họ quyền trên các linh ô uế. \v 8 Ngài dặn họ đừng mang gì theo khi lên đường ngoài một cây gậy: không đồ ăn, không túi hành lý, không tiền trong thắt lưng. \v 9 Họ phải mang dép. Ngài lại dặn: "Đừng mặc thêm áo thứ hai."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu gọi nhóm Mười Hai đến. Ngài bắt đầu sai họ đi, mỗi lần hai người. Ngài ban cho họ quyền trên các tà linh. \v 8 Ngài dặn họ: "Khi đi đường, các con đừng mang theo gì cả, chỉ mang một cây gậy thôi. Đừng mang đồ ăn, túi xách hay tiền bạc. \v 9 Hãy mang dép, nhưng đừng mang thêm áo."

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 열둘을 불러 모으신다. 그리고 그들을 둘씩 둘씩 보내기 시작하셨고, 그들에게 더러운 영들을 [다스리는] 권한을 주셨다. \v 8 그리고 길을 [떠날 때에] 지팡이 하나 말고는 아무것도 가지고 가지 말라고 그들에게 명령하셨다. 빵도, 자루도, 허리띠에 동전도 [가지고 가지 말고], \v 9 신발은 신고 [가라고 하셨다]. 그리고 "속옷 두 벌을 입지 마라."
ko.B: 예수께서 열두 제자를 불러 둘씩 짝지어 보내기 시작하시며, 그들에게 더러운 영들을 다스리는 권한을 주셨다. \v 8 그리고 길을 떠날 때 지팡이 하나 말고는 아무것도 가지고 가지 말라고 이르셨다. 먹을 것도, 자루도, 허리춤에 돈도 가지고 가지 말라고 하셨다. \v 9 신발은 신고 가라고 하셨다. 그리고 "옷을 두 벌 껴입지 마라" 하고 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 열두 제자를 함께 부르셨다. 그리고 그들을 두 사람씩 보내기 시작하셨다. 예수께서는 그들에게 악한 영들을 다스리는 권한을 주셨다. \v 8 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "길을 떠날 때 지팡이 하나 말고는 아무것도 가져가지 마라. 먹을 것도, 가방도, 돈도 가져가지 마라. \v 9 신발은 신고 가거라. 그러나 여벌 옷은 가져가지 마라."

es.L: Y llama a los doce, y comenzó a enviarlos de dos en dos, y les daba autoridad sobre los espíritus impuros; \v 8 y les mandó que no llevaran nada para el camino, sino solo un bastón: ni pan, ni alforja, ni [monedas de] cobre en el cinto, \v 9 sino que fueran calzados con sandalias; y [les dijo]: «No {{plural_you:se pongan|os pongáis}} dos túnicas».
es.B: Llamó a los Doce y comenzó a enviarlos de dos en dos, dándoles autoridad sobre los espíritus impuros. \v 8 Les ordenó que no llevaran nada para el viaje excepto un bastón: ni comida, ni bolsa de viaje, ni monedas en el cinturón. \v 9 Debían ir calzados con sandalias. «Y no {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} una túnica de repuesto», les dijo.
es.R: Jesús reunió a los Doce. Comenzó a enviarlos de dos en dos, y les dio poder sobre los espíritus malignos. \v 8 Les dijo: «No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} nada para el viaje, excepto un bastón. No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} comida, ni bolsa, ni dinero. \v 9 {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} sandalias, pero no {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} ropa de más».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appelle à [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] les douze, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à les envoyer deux par deux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur donnait autorité sur les esprits impurs ; \v 8 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ordonna de ne rien prendre pour la route, sinon un bâton seulement : ni pain, ni sac, ni [monnaie de] cuivre dans la ceinture, \v 9 mais d’être chaussés de sandales ; et : « Ne mettez pas deux tuniques. »
fr.B: Il appela les Douze auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et commença à les envoyer deux par deux, en leur donnant autorité sur les esprits impurs. \v 8 Il leur recommanda de ne rien emporter pour le voyage, sauf un bâton : ni nourriture, ni sac, ni argent dans la ceinture. \v 9 Ils devaient être chaussés de sandales. « Et ne portez pas deux tuniques », ajouta-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}.
fr.R: Jésus a appelé les Douze. Il a commencé à les envoyer deux par deux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a donné le pouvoir de chasser les esprits mauvais. \v 8 Il leur a dit : « Pour le voyage, ne prenez rien avec vous, sauf un bâton de marche. Ne prenez pas de nourriture, pas de sac, pas d’argent. \v 9 Mettez des sandales, mais ne prenez pas de vêtements de rechange. »

sw.L: Na anawaita wale kumi na wawili [waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], akaanza kuwatuma wawili wawili, akawa akiwapa mamlaka juu ya roho wachafu; \v 8 akawaagiza wasichukue chochote kwa ajili ya njia isipokuwa fimbo tu: wala mkate, wala mkoba, wala sarafu za shaba mshipini, \v 9 bali wavae ndara; na, "Msivae kanzu mbili."
sw.B: Akawaita wale Kumi na Wawili {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akaanza kuwatuma wawili wawili, akiwapa mamlaka juu ya roho wachafu. \v 8 Akawaagiza wasichukue chochote kwa safari isipokuwa fimbo ya kutembelea: wasichukue chakula, wala mkoba wa msafiri, wala fedha mishipini mwao. \v 9 Walitakiwa wavae ndara. Akasema, "Wala msivae kanzu ya pili."
sw.R: Yesu aliwaita wale Kumi na Wawili pamoja. Akaanza kuwatuma wawili wawili, na akawapa uwezo juu ya roho waovu. \v 8 Akawaambia, "Msichukue kitu chochote kwa safari isipokuwa fimbo ya kutembelea. Msichukue chakula, wala mkoba, wala fedha. \v 9 Vaeni ndara, lakini msichukue nguo za ziada."

decisions.choice: the twelve: the group Jesus appointed in 3:14-19
decisions.reason: Mark uses the number as the name of the group.

decisions.choice: two by two: in pairs
decisions.reason: Pairs could help each other, and two witnesses made a message stand (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: take nothing but a staff: they are to travel light and depend on the people who take them in
alternatives: they were to be poor forever
decisions.reason: No food, no bag for gifts, no money: they must rely on God and on hospitality (6:10). Sandals and a staff are what one needs to walk.

decisions.choice: bag: a traveler's bag for food or gifts; copper: small coins, carried in the belt
decisions.reason: A belt or sash was folded to hold coins.

decisions.choice: do not put on: the sentence moves from reported instructions to Jesus' own words
decisions.reason: Mark changes from "he instructed them that" to a direct command in the middle of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the Twelve
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable capitalize the number when it serves as the group's name. Literal keeps the plain word.

decisions.choice: direct speech throughout
alternatives: he instructed them that they should take nothing
decisions.reason: Readable gives all the instructions as Jesus' own words, since the Greek ends in direct speech.

decisions.choice: "mười hai [người]" (L); "nhóm Mười Hai" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Twelve is the name of the group Jesus appointed in 3:14-19 (meaning decision). Vietnamese needs a noun after a number, so Literal brackets "người"; Balanced and Readable make it a name with "nhóm" and capitals, as the English writes "the Twelve".

decisions.choice: "linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5: lowercase "linh" for a spirit that is not the Holy Spirit, with "ô uế" for Mark's "unclean"; Readable says "tà linh" (evil spirit), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "các con" for the Twelve
decisions.reason: The style guide's form of address for Jesus speaking to his disciples, used through the chapter (6:10-11, 6:31, 6:37-38, 6:50).

decisions.choice: "열둘" (L); "열두 제자" (B, R); "권한" for authority
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 3:14 and 4:10: Literal keeps Mark's "the twelve"; Balanced and Readable say who they are, as Korean needs a noun. "권한" is authority given by someone, as at 3:15.

decisions.choice: "속옷" (L); "옷" (B); "여벌 옷" (R) for chiton
decisions.reason: "속옷" is the word of the Korean John 19:23 for the tunic worn next to the body, so Literal keeps it; today it suggests underwear, so Balanced and Readable say only that they must not take a second garment.

decisions.choice: espíritus impuros (L, B); espíritus malignos (R)
decisions.reason: "Impuro" says in plain modern Spanish what the Greek adjective says: the spirit makes a person unclean before God. "Inmundo" is the older word. As in English, Readable says "malignos".

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the Twelve, so each plural "you" and its verb is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: ni pain, ni [monnaie de] cuivre (L); ni nourriture, ni argent (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bread and the copper coins of the Greek, bracketing the word French needs; Balanced and Readable say what they stand for, food and money (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: esprits impurs (L, B); esprits mauvais (R); autorité (L, B); pouvoir (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5: "esprit impur" at Literal and Balanced, "esprit mauvais" at Readable; Readable says what the authority was for, "le pouvoir de chasser".

decisions.choice: ndara; kanzu
decisions.reason: "Ndara" are open sandals, where "viatu" would be any shoes. The tunic is "kanzu", the long garment worn next to the body, which is what the Greek names; "joho" is an outer robe.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν, ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Wherever you enter into a house, there remain until you go out from there.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you go out from there.
en.B: He told them, "When you go into a house, stay in it until you leave that town.
en.R: He said, "When someone lets you stay in their house, stay there until you leave that town.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Hễ các con vào nhà nào, hãy ở lại đó cho đến khi các con rời khỏi nơi ấy.
vi.B: Ngài dặn họ: "Khi vào nhà nào, các con hãy ở lại nhà đó cho đến khi rời thành ấy.
vi.R: Ngài nói: "Khi có người cho các con ở trọ trong nhà mình, hãy ở lại nhà đó cho đến khi các con rời thị trấn ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "어디서든지 너희가 어떤 집에 들어가거든, 거기서 떠날 때까지 그곳에 머물러라.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "어느 집에 들어가든지, 그 고을을 떠날 때까지 그 집에 머물러라.
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "누가 너희를 자기 집에 맞아들이면, 그 마을을 떠날 때까지 그 집에 머물러라.

es.L: Y les decía: «Dondequiera que {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una casa, {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} allí hasta que {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}} de allí.
es.B: Les dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una casa, {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} en ella hasta que {{plural_you:se vayan|os vayáis}} de ese pueblo.
es.R: Les dijo: «Cuando alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} reciba en su casa, {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} allí hasta que {{plural_you:se vayan|os vayáis}} de ese pueblo.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « Où que vous entriez dans une maison, restez-y jusqu’à ce que vous partiez de là.
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Quand vous entrez dans une maison, restez-y jusqu’à votre départ de la ville.
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Quand quelqu’un vous reçoit dans sa maison, restez chez lui jusqu’à ce que vous quittiez la ville.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaambia, "Popote mtakapoingia katika nyumba, kaeni humo hadi mtakapotoka mahali pale.
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Mkiingia katika nyumba yoyote, kaeni humo mpaka mtakapoondoka katika mji ule.
sw.R: Akawaambia, "Mtu akiwakaribisha nyumbani kwake, kaeni humo mpaka mtakapoondoka katika mji ule.

decisions.choice: until you go out from there: until you leave the town
decisions.reason: "There" points to the place, not the house: they are to stay in one house for the whole visit.

decisions.choice: stay in one house: do not move around looking for better lodging
decisions.reason: The guest was to accept the first welcome given and not shame the host by leaving for a better offer.

decisions.choice: that town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the place that "there" refers to.

decisions.choice: "머무르다" for meno
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "머무르다" for meno in every sense, as the Korean John does (1:38-39; 15:4-10).

source.text: καὶ ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν, ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And whatever place not receives you nor they hear you, going out from there shake off the dust the [one] under the feet of you for a testimony to them.

en.L: And whatever place does not receive you, and they do not listen to you, as you go out from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet as a testimony to them."
en.B: Where people will not take you in or hear what you say, shake off the dust from under your feet as you go, as a witness against them."
en.R: If the people of a town will not take you in or listen to what you say, leave that town. As you go, shake the dust off your feet. That will be a warning to them."

vi.L: Và nơi nào không tiếp nhận các con, và người ta không nghe các con, khi ra khỏi đó, hãy giũ bụi dưới chân các con để làm chứng cho họ."
vi.B: Nơi nào người ta không tiếp đón các con, cũng không nghe các con, thì khi ra đi, hãy giũ bụi dưới chân mình để làm chứng nghịch lại họ."
vi.R: Nếu người trong thị trấn nào không tiếp đón các con và không chịu nghe các con nói, hãy rời khỏi thị trấn đó. Khi đi, hãy giũ bụi khỏi chân mình. Đó là lời cảnh cáo cho họ."

ko.L: 그리고 어느 곳이든 너희를 맞아들이지 않고 [사람들이] 너희 말을 듣지 않거든, 거기서 나갈 때에 너희 발밑의 먼지를 털어 버려서 그들에게 증언이 되게 하여라."
ko.B: 어디서든 사람들이 너희를 맞아들이지 않고 너희 말을 듣지 않거든, 그곳을 떠날 때 발밑의 먼지를 털어 버려라. 그것이 그들을 고발하는 증언이 될 것이다."
ko.R: 어떤 마을 사람들이 너희를 맞아들이지 않거나 너희 말을 듣지 않으면, 그 마을을 떠나거라. 떠날 때에 발에 묻은 먼지를 털어 버려라. 그것이 그들에게 경고가 될 것이다."

es.L: Y en cualquier lugar que no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciba ni {{plural_you:los|os}} escuchen, al salir de allí, {{plural_you:sacudan|sacudid}} el polvo que está debajo de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pies, como testimonio para ellos».
es.B: Y si en algún lugar no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciben ni {{plural_you:los|os}} escuchan, {{plural_you:sacúdanse|sacudíos}} el polvo de los pies al salir, como testimonio contra ellos».
es.R: Si la gente de un pueblo no {{plural_you:los|os}} recibe ni {{plural_you:los|os}} escucha, {{plural_you:váyanse|idos}} de ese pueblo. Al salir, {{plural_you:sacúdanse|sacudíos}} el polvo de los pies. Eso les servirá de advertencia».

fr.L: Et quel que soit l’endroit qui ne vous reçoit pas et [où] l’on ne vous écoute pas, en sortant de là, secouez la poussière qui est sous vos pieds, en témoignage pour eux. »
fr.B: Et si, quelque part, on refuse de vous accueillir et de vous écouter, secouez en partant la poussière de vos pieds : ce sera un témoignage contre eux. »
fr.R: Si les gens d’une ville ne veulent pas vous recevoir ou vous écouter, quittez cette ville. En partant, secouez la poussière de vos pieds. Ce sera un avertissement pour eux. »

sw.L: Na mahali popote wasipowapokea ninyi wala kuwasikiliza, mnapotoka huko, kung'uteni vumbi lililo chini ya miguu yenu, liwe ushuhuda kwao."
sw.B: Mahali ambapo watu hawatawakaribisha wala kusikiliza mnachosema, mnapoondoka, kung'uteni vumbi la miguu yenu, liwe ushuhuda dhidi yao."
sw.R: Watu wa mji wowote wasipowakaribisha au kuwasikiliza, ondokeni katika mji huo. Mnapoondoka, kung'uteni vumbi kutoka miguuni mwenu. Hilo litakuwa onyo kwao."

decisions.choice: shake off the dust: a sign of breaking off ties with a place
decisions.reason: The act leaves the place to answer for itself. Paul and Barnabas do it in Acts 13:51.

decisions.choice: a testimony to them: a witness that will stand against them
decisions.reason: The act is a warning that they have heard and refused.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the saying here
alternatives: add: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the saying about Sodom and Gomorrah, as in Matthew 10:15. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: place ... they: the people of that place
decisions.reason: The verb changes to plural because a place receives or listens through its people.

decisions.choice: people (B); the people in a town (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people, as the plural verb does.

decisions.choice: "làm chứng nghịch lại họ" (B); "làm chứng cho họ" (L)
decisions.reason: The testimony will stand against them (meaning decision). Vietnamese "làm chứng cho" would usually mean testifying in someone's favour, so Balanced says "nghịch lại"; Literal keeps the Greek's plain "to them".

decisions.choice: "증언" (L, B); "경고" (R) for martyrion
decisions.reason: "증언" is the Korean John's word for testimony and witness; the meaning decision says it is a witness that will stand against them, which Balanced spells out and Readable calls a warning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: en témoignage pour eux (L); un témoignage contre eux (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "a testimony to them", a witness that will stand against them (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the bare dative; Balanced says "contre eux" so the sense is plain.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα μετανοῶσιν, καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον, καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out they preached that they should repent, \v 13 and demons many they were casting out, and were anointing with oil many sick and were healing [them].

en.L: And they went out and proclaimed that [people] should repent, \v 13 and they were casting out many demons and anointing with oil many who were sick and healing [them].
en.B: So they went out and called people to repent. \v 13 They threw out demon after demon, and many who were sick they anointed with oil and made well.
en.R: So the Twelve went out. They told people to turn away from their sins and turn back to God. \v 13 They forced many demons to leave people. They put olive oil on many sick people and healed them.

vi.L: Và họ ra đi và rao giảng rằng [người ta] phải ăn năn, \v 13 và họ đuổi nhiều quỷ, và xức dầu cho nhiều người bệnh và chữa lành [họ].
vi.B: Vậy họ ra đi, kêu gọi người ta ăn năn. \v 13 Họ đuổi được rất nhiều quỷ, và xức dầu cho nhiều người bệnh, chữa họ được lành.
vi.R: Vậy nhóm Mười Hai ra đi. Họ bảo người ta phải từ bỏ tội lỗi và quay về với Đức Chúa Trời. \v 13 Họ đuổi nhiều quỷ ra khỏi người ta. Họ xức dầu ô-liu cho nhiều người bệnh và chữa lành họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 나가서 회개하라고 선포했다. \v 13 그리고 많은 귀신을 쫓아내고 있었고, 많은 병자에게 기름을 발라 고쳐 주고 있었다.
ko.B: 제자들은 나가서 사람들에게 회개하라고 선포했다. \v 13 그들은 많은 귀신을 쫓아냈고, 많은 병자에게 기름을 발라 고쳐 주었다.
ko.R: 그래서 열두 제자는 길을 떠났다. 그들은 사람들에게 죄에서 돌이켜 하나님께 돌아오라고 전했다. \v 13 그들은 많은 귀신을 사람들에게서 쫓아냈다. 또 많은 병자에게 올리브기름을 발라 주고 병을 고쳐 주었다.

es.L: Y saliendo, proclamaron que se arrepintieran, \v 13 y echaban muchos demonios, y ungían con aceite a muchos enfermos y [los] sanaban.
es.B: Así que salieron y llamaban a la gente a arrepentirse. \v 13 Expulsaban a muchos demonios, y a muchos enfermos los ungían con aceite y los sanaban.
es.R: Entonces los Doce salieron. Decían a la gente que dejaran de pecar y se volvieran a Dios. \v 13 Echaron fuera a muchos demonios. Ponían aceite de oliva a muchos enfermos y los sanaban.

fr.L: Et étant partis, ils proclamèrent qu’on se repente, \v 13 et ils chassaient beaucoup de démons, et ils oignaient d’huile beaucoup de malades et [les] guérissaient.
fr.B: Ils partirent donc et appelèrent les gens à se repentir. \v 13 Ils chassaient de nombreux démons, faisaient des onctions d’huile à beaucoup de malades et les guérissaient.
fr.R: Les Douze sont donc partis. Ils ont dit aux gens de se détourner de leurs péchés et de revenir à Dieu. \v 13 Ils obligeaient beaucoup de démons à sortir des gens. Ils mettaient de l’huile d’olive sur beaucoup de malades, et ils les guérissaient.

sw.L: Nao wakatoka, wakahubiri kwamba [watu] watubu, \v 13 na walikuwa wakitoa pepo wengi, na kuwapaka mafuta wagonjwa wengi na kuwaponya.
sw.B: Basi wakaenda, wakawaita watu watubu. \v 13 Wakatoa pepo wengi, na wakawapaka mafuta wagonjwa wengi, wakawaponya.
sw.R: Basi wale Kumi na Wawili wakaenda. Wakawaambia watu waache dhambi zao na kumrudia Mungu. \v 13 Wakawalazimisha pepo wengi kuwatoka watu. Wakawapaka mafuta ya zeituni wagonjwa wengi, wakawaponya.

decisions.choice: repent: turn from sin back to God
decisions.reason: The same message as John's and Jesus' (1:4, 1:15).

decisions.choice: anointing with oil: oil was used as a medicine and as a sign of God's care
decisions.reason: Olive oil was put on wounds and the sick (Luke 10:34). James 5:14 joins anointing with prayer for the sick.

decisions.choice: were casting out, anointing, healing: they did these things again and again
decisions.reason: The tenses describe repeated work through their mission.

decisions.choice: turn away from their sins and turn back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, as at 1:4.

decisions.choice: threw out (B); forced to leave people (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:34 and 3:15.

decisions.choice: "ăn năn" (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Ăn năn" is the Protestant word for repent; "sám hối" is Catholic and Buddhist. Readable spells out the meaning, turning from sin back to God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "회개하다" (L, B); "죄에서 돌이켜 하나님께 돌아오다" (R); "올리브기름" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 1:4 and 1:15 settle for the book. Readable names the oil, since "기름" alone suggests cooking or machine oil to a young reader.

decisions.choice: proclamaron que se arrepintieran, with no supplied [people]
decisions.reason: The Spanish verb shows its plural subject, so Literal needs none of the English brackets here.

decisions.choice: se repentir
decisions.reason: "Se repentir" names turning from sin, as the Greek does (meaning decision m1); "se convertir" now suggests changing religion. Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: the imperfect in Readable (obligeaient, mettaient, guérissaient)
decisions.reason: These things happened again and again (meaning decision m3); French says so with the imperfect even in Readable, whose other narration is in the passé composé.

source.text: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης, φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: And heard King Herod, for well known became the name of him, and they were saying, John the [one] baptizing has been raised from [the] dead, and because of this are at work the powers in him;

en.L: And King Herod heard [of it], for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name had become well known, and they were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from [the] dead, and because of this the powers are at work in him."
en.B: King Herod heard about it, for Jesus' name had become widely known. People were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead. That is why these powers are at work in him."
en.R: King Herod heard about all this, because people everywhere now knew about Jesus. Some were saying, "John the Baptizer has come back from the dead! That is why he can do these miracles."

vi.L: Và vua Hê-rốt nghe [biết], vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã trở nên nổi tiếng, và người ta nói rằng: "Giăng, người làm báp-têm, đã được khiến sống lại từ cõi chết, và vì thế các quyền năng đang hành động trong ông ấy."
vi.B: Vua Hê-rốt nghe nói về việc ấy, vì danh tiếng Đức Giê-xu đã lan rộng. Người ta nói: "Giăng, người làm báp-têm, đã sống lại từ cõi chết. Vì thế mà các quyền năng ấy đang hành động qua ông."
vi.R: Vua Hê-rốt nghe biết mọi chuyện ấy, vì bây giờ khắp nơi ai cũng biết về Đức Giê-xu. Có người nói: "Giăng Báp-tít đã sống lại từ cõi chết! Vì thế ông ấy mới làm được những phép lạ này."

ko.L: 그리고 헤롯 왕이 [이 소문을] 들었다. 그분의 이름이 널리 알려졌기 때문이다. 그리고 [사람들이] 말하고 있었다. "세례를 주는 요한이 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아났다. 그래서 그 능력들이 그 사람 안에서 일하고 있다."
ko.B: 헤롯 왕이 이 소문을 들었다. 예수의 이름이 널리 알려졌기 때문이다. 사람들은 "세례자 요한이 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아났다. 그래서 그에게서 이런 능력이 나타나는 것이다" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 헤롯 왕도 이 모든 일을 들었다. 이제 예수에 대해 모르는 사람이 없었기 때문이다. 어떤 사람들은 "세례자 요한이 죽었다가 다시 살아났다! 그래서 그가 이런 놀라운 일들을 할 수 있는 것이다!" 하고 말했다.

es.L: Y oyó [de ello] el rey Herodes, porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre se había hecho conocido, y decían: «Juan el que bautiza ha resucitado de entre [los] muertos, y por eso actúan en él los poderes».
es.B: El rey Herodes se enteró de esto, porque el nombre de Jesús se había hecho muy conocido. La gente decía: «Juan el que bautizaba ha resucitado de entre los muertos. Por eso actúan en él estos poderes».
es.R: El rey Herodes oyó hablar de todo esto, porque ahora todo el mundo conocía a Jesús. Algunos decían: «¡Juan el que bautizaba ha vuelto de entre los muertos! Por eso puede hacer estos milagros».

fr.L: Et le roi Hérode [en] entendit parler, car {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom était devenu célèbre, et l’on disait : « Jean le Baptiseur est ressuscité d’entre les morts, et c’est pourquoi les puissances agissent en lui. »
fr.B: Le roi Hérode en entendit parler, car le nom de Jésus était devenu célèbre. On disait : « Jean le Baptiseur est ressuscité d’entre les morts ; voilà pourquoi ces puissances agissent en lui. »
fr.R: Le roi Hérode a entendu parler de tout cela, parce que tout le monde connaissait maintenant Jésus. Certains disaient : « Jean le Baptiseur est revenu à la vie ! C’est pour ça qu’il peut faire ces miracles. »

sw.L: Na mfalme Herode akasikia, kwa maana jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} lilikuwa limejulikana sana, nao walikuwa wakisema, "Yohana abatizaye amefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, na kwa sababu hiyo nguvu hizi zinatenda kazi ndani yake."
sw.B: Mfalme Herode alisikia habari hizi, kwa maana jina la Yesu lilikuwa limejulikana kila mahali. Watu walikuwa wakisema, "Yohana Mbatizaji amefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu. Ndiyo sababu nguvu hizi zinatenda kazi ndani yake."
sw.R: Mfalme Herode alisikia habari hizi zote, kwa sababu sasa watu kila mahali walimjua Yesu. Baadhi yao walikuwa wakisema, "Yohana Mbatizaji amefufuka kutoka kwa wafu! Ndiyo maana anaweza kufanya miujiza hii."

decisions.choice: King Herod: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, ruler of Galilee and Perea
decisions.reason: Rome gave Antipas the lesser title tetrarch, ruler of part of a kingdom (Luke 3:1). Mark uses the title people gave him. Josephus records that Antipas later lost his land after seeking the title king.

decisions.choice: they were saying, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "he was saying", making this Herod's own opinion, as in 6:16. The SBLGNT reads the plural, which fits the list of opinions in 6:15. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: his name: Jesus' name
decisions.reason: The sentence follows the mission of the Twelve. The fame is Jesus', spread by their work.

decisions.choice: the powers are at work in him: miraculous powers act through him
decisions.reason: People think a prophet returned from the dead would have such powers.

decisions.choice: Jesus' name (B); knew about Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last person named is Herod.

decisions.choice: "Giăng, người làm báp-têm" (L, B); "Giăng Báp-tít" (R)
decisions.reason: Here Mark calls John "the one baptizing", a participle (also 6:24), and in 6:25 "the Baptist", a noun. Literal and Balanced keep the difference, as the English does with "Baptizer" and "Baptist"; Readable uses the familiar name "Giăng Báp-tít" throughout. "Làm báp-têm" is the settled Protestant term; "Tẩy Giả" is Catholic.

decisions.choice: "헤롯 왕"; "세례를 주는 요한" (L); "세례자 요한" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark calls Herod Antipas "king" (meaning decision), and Korean keeps the title. For "John the one baptizing" the Korean Mark 1:4 has "세례를 주는 요한" at Literal and "세례자 요한" at Balanced and Readable; this chapter follows it (6:14, 6:24).

decisions.choice: Juan el que bautiza (L); Juan el que bautizaba (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here and at 6:24 Mark uses a participle, "the one baptizing"; at 6:25 he uses the noun, which Spanish renders "el Bautista". The levels keep the two apart, as the English does with "Baptizer" and "Baptist".

decisions.choice: Jean le Baptiseur (6:14, 6:24); Jean le Baptiste (6:25)
decisions.reason: Mark says "John the one baptizing" here and in 6:24, as in 1:4, but "John the Baptist" with the noun in 6:25 (meaning decision there). French follows the English and the French of Mark 1: "le Baptiseur" for the participle, "le Baptiste" for the noun.

decisions.choice: Yohana abatizaye (L); Yohana Mbatizaji (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark calls John "the one baptizing" here and in 6:24, and "the Baptist" in 6:25. Literal shows the participle with "abatizaye" (who baptizes) and keeps "Mbatizaji" for the noun; Balanced and Readable use the familiar title "Yohana Mbatizaji" throughout, since Swahili has one natural title where English has "Baptizer" and "Baptist".

source.text: ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐστίν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Others but were saying, Elijah he is; others but were saying, A prophet like one of the prophets.

en.L: But others were saying, "He is Elijah." And others were saying, "[He is] a prophet, like one of the prophets."
en.B: Others said, "It is Elijah," and others again, "He is a prophet, one like the prophets of long ago."
en.R: Other people said, "He is Elijah, the prophet who was taken up to heaven long ago." Still others said, "He is a prophet like the great prophets of long ago."

vi.L: Nhưng những người khác nói: "Ông ấy là Ê-li." Những người khác nữa nói: "[Ông ấy là] một nhà tiên tri, như một trong các nhà tiên tri."
vi.B: Những người khác lại nói: "Đó là Ê-li." Còn có người nói: "Ông ấy là một nhà tiên tri, giống như các nhà tiên tri thời xưa."
vi.R: Những người khác nói: "Ông ấy là Ê-li, nhà tiên tri đã được cất lên trời từ xưa." Còn những người khác nữa thì nói: "Ông ấy là một nhà tiên tri giống như các nhà tiên tri lớn ngày xưa."

ko.L: 그러나 다른 사람들은 "그는 엘리야다" 하고 말하고 있었다. 또 다른 사람들은 "[그는] 예언자들 가운데 하나와 같은 예언자다" 하고 말하고 있었다.
ko.B: 또 어떤 사람들은 "그는 엘리야다" 하고, 또 어떤 사람들은 "그는 옛 예언자들 가운데 하나와 같은 예언자다" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 다른 사람들은 "그는 오래전에 하늘로 올라간 예언자 엘리야다" 하고 말했다. 또 다른 사람들은 "그는 옛날의 위대한 예언자들과 같은 예언자다" 하고 말했다.

es.L: Pero otros decían: «Es Elías». Y otros decían: «[Es] un profeta, como uno de los profetas».
es.B: Otros decían: «Es Elías». Y otros: «Es un profeta, como los profetas de antes».
es.R: Otros decían: «Es Elías, el profeta que hace mucho tiempo fue llevado al cielo». Y otros decían: «Es un profeta como los grandes profetas de hace mucho tiempo».

fr.L: Mais d’autres disaient : « C’est Élie. » Et d’autres disaient : « [C’est] un prophète, comme l’un des prophètes. »
fr.B: D’autres disaient : « C’est Élie », et d’autres encore : « C’est un prophète, pareil aux prophètes d’autrefois. »
fr.R: D’autres disaient : « C’est Élie, le prophète qui a été enlevé au ciel il y a très longtemps. » D’autres encore disaient : « C’est un prophète comme les grands prophètes d’autrefois. »

sw.L: Lakini wengine walikuwa wakisema, "Ni Eliya." Na wengine walikuwa wakisema, "[Ni] nabii, kama mmoja wa manabii."
sw.B: Wengine walisema, "Ni Eliya," na wengine tena, "Ni nabii, kama wale manabii wa zamani."
sw.R: Watu wengine walisema, "Yeye ni Eliya, yule nabii aliyechukuliwa mbinguni zamani." Wengine walisema, "Yeye ni nabii kama wale manabii wakuu wa zamani."

decisions.choice: Elijah: the prophet God promised to send before the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:5 promised that Elijah would come again. Elijah had not died but was taken up (2 Kings 2:11).

decisions.choice: like one of the prophets: a prophet of the old kind
alternatives: one of the old prophets come back to life
decisions.reason: These people do not say he is a prophet returned, only that he is like them.

decisions.choice: the prophet who was taken up to heaven long ago
decisions.reason: Readable explains who Elijah was.

decisions.choice: People speak of Jesus as "그", with no honorific
decisions.reason: The speakers take him for John, Elijah or a prophet, not for the one the narrator honours; the narrator keeps "께서" for Jesus throughout.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἔλεγεν· Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάννην, οὗτος ἠγέρθη.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard but Herod was saying, Whom I beheaded, John, this one has been raised.

en.L: But when Herod heard [of it], he was saying, "John, whom I beheaded, this one has been raised."
en.B: But when Herod heard of it, he said, "It is John, the man I beheaded. He has been raised!"
en.R: But when Herod heard about it, he said, "It is John! I had his head cut off, but now he has come back to life!"

vi.L: Nhưng Hê-rốt nghe [vậy] thì nói: "Giăng, người mà chính ta đã chém đầu, ông ấy đã sống lại."
vi.B: Nhưng khi nghe vậy, Hê-rốt nói: "Đó chính là Giăng, người mà ta đã chém đầu. Ông ấy đã sống lại!"
vi.R: Nhưng khi Hê-rốt nghe những điều ấy, ông ta nói: "Đó là Giăng! Chính ta đã cho chém đầu ông ấy, vậy mà bây giờ ông ấy đã sống lại!"

ko.L: 그러나 헤롯은 듣고 말하고 있었다. "내가 목 벤 요한, 그 사람이 살아났다."
ko.B: 그러나 헤롯은 이 말을 듣고 말했다. "내가 목을 벤 그 요한이다. 그가 살아났다!"
ko.R: 그러나 헤롯은 그 말을 듣고 말했다. "요한이다! 내가 그의 목을 베게 했는데, 그가 다시 살아났구나!"

es.L: Pero al oír[lo], Herodes decía: «Juan, al que yo decapité, este ha resucitado».
es.B: Pero cuando Herodes lo oyó, dijo: «Es Juan, el hombre al que yo decapité. ¡Ha resucitado!».
es.R: Pero cuando Herodes oyó esto, dijo: «¡Es Juan! Yo mandé que le cortaran la cabeza, ¡y ahora ha vuelto a vivir!».

fr.L: Mais Hérode, l’ayant appris, disait : « Celui que moi j’ai décapité, Jean, celui-là est ressuscité. »
fr.B: Mais Hérode, apprenant cela, dit : « C’est Jean, celui que j’ai fait décapiter. Il est ressuscité ! »
fr.R: Mais quand Hérode a entendu parler de tout cela, il a dit : « C’est Jean ! Je lui ai fait couper la tête, mais maintenant il est revenu à la vie ! »

sw.L: Lakini Herode aliposikia, alikuwa akisema, "Yohana, ambaye mimi nilimkata kichwa, huyo amefufuliwa."
sw.B: Lakini Herode aliposikia habari hizo, alisema, "Ni Yohana, yule mtu niliyemkata kichwa. Amefufuliwa!"
sw.R: Lakini Herode aliposikia habari hizo, alisema, "Ni Yohana! Niliamuru akatwe kichwa, lakini sasa amefufuka!"

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, Herod knows he is to blame
decisions.reason: Herod adds the pronoun for emphasis: I myself had him killed.

decisions.choice: this one: Herod settles on one view
decisions.reason: Of the opinions in 6:14-15, Herod takes the first.

decisions.choice: had his head cut off
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words, and "had" shows that Herod gave the order.

decisions.choice: "ta" for Herod speaking, lowercase, with no setting
decisions.reason: A king speaks of himself as "ta" in Vietnamese storytelling; "trẫm" is archaic court language. It is Herod, not Jesus, so it takes no deity_pronoun span. "Chính ta" keeps the emphatic "I" (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: yo decapité
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves out the subject pronoun, so writing "yo" shows the emphasis of the Greek "I" (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: moi j’ai décapité (L); j’ai fait décapiter (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Herod’s emphatic "I" and the plain verb (meaning decision m1); Balanced says "fait décapiter", which is how French says that a king had it done by others (6:27).

source.text: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν·

records.literal_gloss: Himself for Herod having sent seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias the wife of Philip the brother of him, because her he had married;

en.L: For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her;
en.B: It was Herod himself who had sent men to seize John and had tied him up in prison. He did it on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, since he had married her.
en.R: Some time before this, Herod had sent soldiers to arrest John. They tied him up and put him in prison. Herod did this because of Herodias. She had been the wife of Herod's brother Philip, but Herod had married her.

vi.L: Vì chính Hê-rốt đã sai người bắt Giăng và xiềng ông trong ngục, vì cớ Hê-rô-đia, vợ của Phi-líp, anh em mình, vì ông ta đã cưới bà ấy;
vi.B: Số là chính Hê-rốt đã sai người đi bắt Giăng và xiềng ông trong ngục. Hê-rốt làm vậy vì Hê-rô-đia, vợ của Phi-líp, anh em mình, vì ông ta đã cưới bà.
vi.R: Trước đó, Hê-rốt đã sai lính đi bắt Giăng. Họ trói ông lại và bỏ vào ngục. Hê-rốt làm vậy là vì Hê-rô-đia. Bà vốn là vợ của Phi-líp, anh em của Hê-rốt, nhưng Hê-rốt đã cưới bà.

ko.L: 헤롯 자신이 [사람을] 보내어 요한을 붙잡고 감옥에 묶어 두었던 것이다. 그의 형제 빌립의 아내 헤로디아 때문이었는데, 그가 그 여자와 결혼했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 바로 헤롯 자신이 사람들을 보내어 요한을 붙잡고 감옥에 묶어 두었던 것이다. 그것은 헤롯의 형제 빌립의 아내 헤로디아 때문이었다. 헤롯이 그 여자와 결혼했던 것이다.
ko.R: 이보다 얼마 전에 헤롯은 군인들을 보내 요한을 잡아 오게 했다. 그들은 요한을 묶어 감옥에 가두었다. 헤롯이 그렇게 한 것은 헤로디아 때문이었다. 헤로디아는 원래 헤롯의 형제 빌립의 아내였는데, 헤롯이 그 여자와 결혼했다.

es.L: Porque el mismo Herodes había enviado a prender a Juan y lo había encadenado en la cárcel a causa de Herodías, la mujer de Felipe su hermano, porque se había casado con ella;
es.B: Es que Herodes mismo había mandado arrestar a Juan y lo había encadenado en la cárcel. Lo hizo por causa de Herodías, la esposa de su hermano Felipe, con quien él se había casado.
es.R: Tiempo atrás, Herodes había enviado soldados a arrestar a Juan. Lo ataron y lo metieron en la cárcel. Herodes hizo esto por causa de Herodías. Ella había sido la esposa de Felipe, el hermano de Herodes, pero Herodes se había casado con ella.

fr.L: Car Hérode lui-même avait envoyé saisir Jean et l’avait enchaîné en prison, à cause d’Hérodiade, la femme de Philippe son frère, parce qu’il l’avait épousée ;
fr.B: C’était en effet Hérode lui-même qui avait fait arrêter Jean et l’avait fait enchaîner en prison. Il avait agi ainsi à cause d’Hérodiade, la femme de son frère Philippe, qu’il avait épousée.
fr.R: Quelque temps avant, Hérode avait envoyé des soldats arrêter Jean. Ils l’avaient attaché et mis en prison. Hérode avait fait cela à cause d’Hérodiade. Elle avait été la femme de Philippe, le frère d’Hérode, mais Hérode l’avait épousée.

sw.L: Kwa maana Herode mwenyewe alikuwa ametuma [watu] akamkamata Yohana, akamfunga gerezani kwa ajili ya Herodia, mke wa Filipo ndugu yake, kwa sababu alikuwa amemwoa;
sw.B: Herode mwenyewe ndiye aliyekuwa ametuma watu kumkamata Yohana na kumfunga gerezani. Alifanya hivyo kwa sababu ya Herodia, mke wa ndugu yake Filipo, kwa kuwa alikuwa amemwoa.
sw.R: Muda fulani kabla ya hapo, Herode alikuwa ametuma askari wamkamate Yohana. Wakamfunga, wakamtia gerezani. Herode alifanya hivyo kwa sababu ya Herodia. Herodia alikuwa mke wa Filipo, ndugu yake Herode, lakini Herode alikuwa amemwoa.

decisions.choice: for: the story goes back to explain what happened to John earlier
decisions.reason: Mark tells John's death as a flashback, from 6:17 to 6:29.

decisions.choice: Herodias: Herod's niece, first married to his half-brother
decisions.reason: Josephus records that Herodias left her first husband, a half-brother of Antipas, to marry Antipas. He calls that brother Herod; Mark calls him Philip. The family used the name Herod for many of its men, and one man could have had both names.

decisions.choice: in prison: in one of Herod's fortresses
decisions.reason: Josephus says John was held at Machaerus, a fortress east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: Some time before this
decisions.reason: Readable marks the flashback plainly.

decisions.choice: "ông" for John, "ông ta" for Herod
decisions.reason: Both men need a pronoun. John, the righteous prophet, is "ông"; Herod is "ông ta", a little more distant, which also keeps it clear who does what in 6:17-28.

decisions.choice: Protestant name forms "헤롯", "헤로디아", "빌립"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (style guide, section 5); the Catholic forms are the alternatives.

decisions.choice: Herode, Herodia, Filipo
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Swahili forms.

source.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.

records.literal_gloss: Was saying for John to Herod, Not it is lawful for you to have the wife of the brother of you.

en.L: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
en.B: John had kept telling Herod, "The law does not allow you to have your brother's wife."
en.R: John had told Herod again and again, "God's law says you must not marry your brother's wife."

vi.L: Vì Giăng đã nói với Hê-rốt: "Vua không được phép lấy vợ của anh em mình."
vi.B: Giăng đã nhiều lần nói với Hê-rốt: "Luật pháp không cho phép vua lấy vợ của anh em mình."
vi.R: Giăng cứ nói đi nói lại với Hê-rốt: "Luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời cấm vua cưới vợ của anh em mình."

ko.L: 요한이 헤롯에게 "왕께서 왕의 형제의 아내를 차지하시는 것은 허락되지 않습니다" 하고 말해 왔기 때문이다.
ko.B: 요한이 헤롯에게 "왕께서 형제의 아내를 차지하시는 것은 율법이 허락하지 않습니다" 하고 거듭 말해 왔던 것이다.
ko.R: 요한은 헤롯에게 여러 번 이렇게 말했었다. "하나님의 율법에 따르면, 왕께서는 형제의 아내와 결혼하시면 안 됩니다."

es.L: Porque Juan le decía a Herodes: «No te es lícito tener la mujer de tu hermano».
es.B: Juan le había estado diciendo a Herodes: «La ley no te permite tener a la esposa de tu hermano».
