vi.R: Vậy dân chúng ngồi xuống thành từng nhóm. Có nhóm một trăm người, có nhóm năm mươi người.

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 밭이랑처럼 한 줄 한 줄, 백 명씩 쉰 명씩 기대어 앉았다.
ko.B: 그래서 사람들은 백 명씩, 또는 쉰 명씩 꽃밭처럼 가지런히 무리 지어 앉았다.
ko.R: 그래서 사람들이 무리를 지어 앉았다. 백 명씩 앉은 무리도 있었고, 쉰 명씩 앉은 무리도 있었다.

es.L: Y se recostaron en cuadros, cuadro por cuadro, de cien en cien y de cincuenta en cincuenta.
es.B: Y se sentaron en grupos, como los cuadros de un huerto, de cien y de cincuenta.
es.R: Así que la gente se sentó en grupos. Algunos grupos eran de cien personas, y otros de cincuenta.

fr.L: Et ils s’allongèrent, carré par carré, par cent et par cinquante.
fr.B: Ils s’assirent donc par groupes, comme les carrés d’un jardin, par cent et par cinquante.
fr.R: Les gens se sont donc assis par groupes. Certains groupes avaient cent personnes, d’autres cinquante.

sw.L: Nao wakaketi matuta matuta, mia mia na hamsini hamsini.
sw.B: Basi wakaketi katika makundi kama matuta ya bustani, makundi ya watu mia mia na hamsini hamsini.
sw.R: Basi watu wakaketi katika makundi. Makundi mengine yalikuwa na watu mia moja, na mengine watu hamsini.

decisions.choice: plots: garden beds, a picture of neat groups
decisions.reason: The word means a garden bed. The groups on the grass looked like rows of plants.

decisions.choice: hundreds and fifties: like Israel ordered in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Moses set leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens (Exodus 18:21, 18:25).

decisions.choice: like the plots of a garden
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture as a simile.

decisions.choice: "luống" (garden beds)
decisions.reason: Mark's word is the plots of a garden, a picture of neat groups (meaning decision). Literal keeps the doubled "từng luống, từng luống"; Balanced makes the picture a comparison, as the English does.

decisions.choice: cuadros (L); como los cuadros de un huerto (B)
decisions.reason: "Cuadro" is the Spanish word for a bed in a garden, so Literal can keep the Greek picture (meaning decision) and Balanced makes it explicit, as the English does.

decisions.choice: cien, cincuenta in words
decisions.reason: Round numbers inside the phrase read naturally in words in Spanish, as the Spanish of John writes "doscientos denarios".

decisions.choice: carré par carré (L); comme les carrés d’un jardin (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a garden bed (meaning decision m1); French "carré" is the usual name of a garden plot, so Literal can keep the picture and Balanced only adds the garden. Readable writes "cent" in words, as the French guide asks for numbers up to a hundred.

decisions.choice: matuta matuta (L); kama matuta ya bustani (B)
decisions.reason: "Matuta" are the raised beds of a garden, the picture the Greek word gives; Swahili repeats the noun and the numbers ("mia mia, hamsini hamsini") for "by hundreds and by fifties", as the Greek repeats its word.

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἐμέρισεν πᾶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up to the heaven he blessed and broke the loaves and was giving to the disciples so that they might set before them, and the two fish he divided among all.

en.L: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up to heaven and blessed, and broke the loaves and kept giving [them] to the disciples to set before them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} divided the two fish among all.
en.B: Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, and spoke a blessing. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the loaves and handed them again and again to the disciples to serve to the people. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shared out the two fish among everyone.
en.R: Jesus took the five loaves of bread and the two fish. He looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the loaves into pieces and kept giving them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. They passed them out to the people. He also divided the two fish so that everyone had some.

vi.L: Và cầm lấy năm cái bánh và hai con cá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngước mắt lên trời và chúc phước, rồi bẻ bánh ra và cứ trao cho các môn đồ để họ dọn ra cho [dân chúng], và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chia hai con cá cho mọi người.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu cầm lấy năm cái bánh và hai con cá, ngước mắt lên trời và dâng lời chúc tụng. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bẻ bánh ra, cứ trao cho các môn đồ để họ phân phát cho dân chúng. Ngài cũng chia hai con cá cho mọi người.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu cầm lấy năm cái bánh và hai con cá. Ngài nhìn lên trời và cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về thức ăn. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bẻ bánh ra thành từng miếng và cứ trao cho các môn đồ. Các môn đồ phân phát cho dân chúng. Ngài cũng chia hai con cá cho mọi người đều có phần.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 빵 다섯 개와 물고기 두 마리를 손에 드시고 하늘을 우러러보시며 축복하시고, 빵을 떼어 제자들에게 계속 주시며 그들 앞에 차려 놓게 하셨다. 그리고 물고기 두 마리도 모두에게 나누어 주셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 빵 다섯 개와 물고기 두 마리를 손에 드시고 하늘을 우러러 찬양의 기도를 드리셨다. 그리고 빵을 떼어 제자들에게 거듭 나누어 주시며 사람들에게 차려 주게 하셨다. 물고기 두 마리도 모든 사람에게 나누어 주셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 빵 다섯 개와 물고기 두 마리를 손에 드셨다. 그리고 하늘을 올려다보시며 음식을 주신 하나님께 감사드리셨다. 그다음에 빵을 조각조각 떼어 제자들에게 계속 주셨다. 제자들은 그것을 사람들에게 나누어 주었다. 예수께서는 물고기 두 마리도 나누어 모든 사람이 먹게 하셨다.

es.L: Y tomando los cinco panes y los dos peces, alzando los ojos al cielo, bendijo, y partió los panes y se [los] iba dando a los discípulos para que [se los] sirvieran, y repartió los dos peces entre todos.
es.B: Jesús tomó los cinco panes y los dos pescados, levantó la vista al cielo y pronunció la bendición. Luego partió los panes y se los fue dando una y otra vez a los discípulos para que los sirvieran a la gente. También repartió los dos pescados entre todos.
es.R: Jesús tomó los cinco panes y los dos pescados. Miró al cielo y dio gracias a Dios por la comida. Luego partió los panes en pedazos y se los iba dando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Ellos los repartían entre la gente. También dividió los dos pescados para que todos comieran.

fr.L: Et prenant les cinq pains et les deux poissons, levant les yeux vers le ciel, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} bénit, et rompit les pains, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les donnait aux disciples pour qu’ils les leur présentent ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partagea les deux poissons entre tous.
fr.B: Jésus prit les cinq pains et les deux poissons, leva les yeux vers le ciel et prononça la bénédiction. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rompit les pains et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les donnait au fur et à mesure aux disciples pour qu’ils les servent à la foule. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partagea aussi les deux poissons entre tous.
fr.R: Jésus a pris les cinq pains et les deux poissons. Il a levé les yeux vers le ciel et a remercié Dieu pour cette nourriture. Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rompu les pains en morceaux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les donnait sans arrêt à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Les disciples les distribuaient aux gens. Il a aussi partagé les deux poissons pour que chacun en ait un peu.

sw.L: Naye akiisha kuitwaa ile mikate mitano na wale samaki wawili, akatazama juu mbinguni, akabariki, akaimega mikate, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi ili wawaandalie; na wale samaki wawili akawagawia wote.
sw.B: Yesu aliichukua ile mikate mitano na samaki wawili, akatazama juu mbinguni, akatamka baraka. Kisha akaimega mikate, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi tena na tena ili wawagawie watu. Na wale samaki wawili akawagawia wote.
sw.R: Yesu aliichukua mikate ile mitano na samaki wale wawili. Akatazama juu mbinguni, akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili ya chakula. Kisha akaimega mikate vipande vipande, akaendelea kuwapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Nao wakawagawia watu. Pia aliwagawanya wale samaki wawili ili kila mtu apate.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised God over the food
alternatives: blessed the bread to change it
decisions.reason: A Jewish meal began with a blessing of God, who gives bread. The verb has no object here.

decisions.choice: took, blessed, broke, gave: the same actions as at the Last Supper
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same four verbs at 14:22.

decisions.choice: kept giving: the bread kept coming from his hands
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures him handing out bread again and again.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the SBLGNT has no "his"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "his disciples". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: thanked God for the food
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the blessing addressed.

decisions.choice: "chúc phước" (L); "dâng lời chúc tụng" (B); "cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus praises God over the food (meaning decision). Literal keeps the Greek "blessed" with "chúc phước", the word for saying a blessing; Balanced makes clear that the praise goes to God; Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does. "Tạ ơn" is kept for the different verb "give thanks" (John 6:11).

decisions.choice: "축복하다" (L); "찬양의 기도를 드리다" (B); "하나님께 감사드리다" (R) for eulogeo
decisions.reason: The verb is to bless, that is, to praise God over the food (meaning decision). Literal keeps "축복하다"; Balanced says it is praise to God, so it is not read as blessing the bread; Readable uses thanks, as the English Readable does. The Korean John 6:11 keeps "감사" for a different verb (eucharisteo).

decisions.choice: rompre les pains
decisions.reason: "Rompre le pain" is the French expression for the action at the Last Supper and in the early church, so every level keeps the echo noted in meaning decision m2.

decisions.choice: aux disciples (L, B)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has no "his" (meaning decision m4), and French needs none, so Literal and Balanced say "aux disciples"; Readable follows the English Readable.

source.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν·

records.literal_gloss: And ate all and were satisfied.

en.L: And all ate and were satisfied.
en.B: They all ate until they were full.
en.R: Everyone ate as much as they wanted.

vi.L: Và mọi người đều ăn và được no nê.
vi.B: Mọi người đều ăn no.
vi.R: Ai cũng được ăn bao nhiêu tùy thích.

ko.L: 그리고 모두가 먹고 배불렀다.
ko.B: 모두 배불리 먹었다.
ko.R: 모든 사람이 먹고 싶은 만큼 먹었다.

es.L: Y comieron todos y se saciaron.
es.B: Todos comieron hasta quedar satisfechos.
es.R: Todos comieron cuanto quisieron.

fr.L: Et tous mangèrent et furent rassasiés.
fr.B: Tous mangèrent à leur faim.
fr.R: Tout le monde a mangé autant qu’il voulait.

sw.L: Na wote wakala na kushiba.
sw.B: Wote walikula mpaka wakashiba.
sw.R: Kila mtu alikula kadiri alivyotaka.

decisions.choice: were satisfied: filled, with nothing lacking
decisions.reason: The verb is used for feeding animals until full, and for people eating their fill.

decisions.choice: all ate and were satisfied: God feeding his people in the wilderness
decisions.reason: God fed Israel with manna in the wilderness (Exodus 16), and Psalm 78:29 says they ate and were well filled.

source.text: καὶ ἦραν κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων.

records.literal_gloss: And they took up broken pieces, of twelve baskets fullnesses, and from the fish.

en.L: And they took up broken pieces, the fill of twelve baskets, and [some] of the fish.
en.B: Then they gathered up twelve baskets full of broken pieces of bread, and of the fish too.
en.R: Afterward they picked up the pieces of bread and fish that were left. There was enough to fill twelve baskets.

vi.L: Và họ nhặt lấy những mẩu bánh, đầy mười hai giỏ, và [một phần] cá.
vi.B: Rồi họ nhặt được mười hai giỏ đầy những mẩu bánh, cùng với cá còn thừa.
vi.R: Sau đó, họ nhặt những miếng bánh và cá còn thừa. Số còn thừa đựng đầy mười hai giỏ.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 조각들, 곧 열두 바구니에 가득한 것과 물고기에서 [남은 것을] 거두었다.
ko.B: 그리고 남은 빵 조각을 거두니 열두 바구니에 가득 찼고, 물고기도 남았다.
ko.R: 그런 뒤에 제자들이 남은 빵과 물고기 조각들을 거두었다. 그것이 열두 바구니에 가득 찼다.

es.L: Y recogieron pedazos, doce cestas llenas, y [también] de los peces.
es.B: Después recogieron doce cestas llenas de pedazos de pan, y también de pescado.
es.R: Después recogieron los pedazos de pan y de pescado que sobraron. Había suficiente para llenar doce cestas.

fr.L: Et ils ramassèrent des morceaux, de quoi remplir douze paniers, et [des restes] des poissons.
fr.B: Ils ramassèrent ensuite douze paniers pleins de morceaux de pain, et aussi des restes de poissons.
fr.R: Après le repas, ils ont ramassé les morceaux de pain et de poisson qui restaient. Il y en avait assez pour remplir douze paniers.

sw.L: Nao wakaokota vipande vilivyomegwa, vikapu kumi na viwili vilivyojaa, na [vipande] vya samaki.
sw.B: Kisha wakakusanya vipande vya mikate vilivyobaki, vikajaa vikapu kumi na viwili, na vipande vya samaki pia.
sw.R: Baadaye wakaokota vipande vya mikate na samaki vilivyobaki. Vilitosha kujaza vikapu kumi na viwili.

decisions.choice: baskets: wicker baskets, the kind carried by travelers
decisions.reason: A different word is used for the larger baskets in 8:8.

decisions.choice: twelve baskets: more left over than there was at the start
decisions.reason: The number may recall the twelve tribes or the twelve apostles; Mark does not explain it.

decisions.choice: they: most likely the disciples
decisions.reason: The disciples served the food, and it is natural that they gathered what was left.

decisions.choice: cestas
decisions.reason: The same word for travelers' baskets as in John 6:13, where the Spanish says "cestas".

source.text: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες.

records.literal_gloss: And were those having eaten the loaves five thousand men.

en.L: And those who ate the loaves were 5,000 men.
en.B: The men who had eaten the loaves numbered 5,000.
en.R: There were 5,000 men who ate the bread.

vi.L: Và những người đã ăn bánh là năm nghìn người đàn ông.
vi.B: Số đàn ông đã ăn bánh là năm nghìn người.
vi.R: Có năm nghìn người đàn ông đã ăn bánh.

ko.L: 그리고 그 빵을 먹은 사람들은 남자가 5,000명이었다.
ko.B: 빵을 먹은 남자들은 5,000명이었다.
ko.R: 빵을 먹은 남자가 5,000명이나 되었다.

es.L: Y los que comieron los panes eran 5000 hombres.
es.B: Los hombres que comieron los panes eran 5000.
es.R: Los hombres que comieron el pan eran 5000.

fr.L: Et ceux qui avaient mangé les pains étaient 5 000 hommes.
fr.B: Ceux qui avaient mangé les pains étaient au nombre de 5 000 hommes.
fr.R: Il y avait 5 000 hommes qui avaient mangé du pain.

sw.L: Na wale walioila mikate walikuwa wanaume elfu tano.
sw.B: Wanaume waliokula mikate ile walikuwa elfu tano.
sw.R: Wanaume waliokula mikate walikuwa elfu tano.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word means men as distinct from women and children. Mark counts the men; Matthew 14:21 says women and children ate as well.

decisions.choice: the loaves, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts do not have "the loaves". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals. "Men" takes no gender setting, because only males are meant.

decisions.choice: "năm nghìn" in words
decisions.reason: The style guide writes numbers in words in running text, where the English uses figures, as the Vietnamese John does for the same number (6:10).

decisions.choice: "남자" with no gender span; "5,000명" in figures
decisions.reason: The Greek word means adult males (meaning decision), as at John 6:10, where the Korean also says "남자들" and writes the number in figures.

decisions.choice: 5000 hombres, no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Greek word means adult males (meaning decision), so "hombres" is not under the setting, as in the Spanish of John 6:10. Spanish writes four-digit numbers without a separator.

decisions.choice: 5~000 hommes, no gender setting
decisions.reason: Mark uses the word for adult males (meaning decision m1), so "hommes" is not under the setting, as in the French John 6:10. Numbers above "cent" are in figures with the French thin space.

decisions.choice: wanaume elfu tano, in words
decisions.reason: The Greek word means adult men, so "wanaume" (men) with no gender span, as in the Swahili of John 6:10. The number is written in words, as Swahili running text writes numbers.

source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν, ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately he compelled the disciples of him to embark into the boat and to go ahead to the other side to Bethsaida, while he himself dismisses the crowd.

en.L: And immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} dismisses the crowd.
en.B: Right away Jesus pressed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to board the boat and cross ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Bethsaida on the other side, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dismissed the crowd.
en.R: Right after that, Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to get into the boat and go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} across the lake to the town of Bethsaida. He stayed behind to send the people home.

vi.L: Và lập tức {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống thuyền và đi trước qua bờ bên kia, đến Bết-sai-đa, trong khi chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giải tán đoàn dân.
vi.B: Ngay sau đó Đức Giê-xu giục các môn đồ xuống thuyền, qua bờ bên kia đến Bết-sai-đa trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, trong khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho dân chúng ra về.
vi.R: Ngay sau đó, Đức Giê-xu bảo các môn đồ xuống thuyền đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua bên kia hồ, đến thị trấn Bết-sai-đa. Ngài ở lại để cho dân chúng về nhà.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 그분이 그분의 제자들을 재촉하여 배에 오르게 하시고, 자기가 무리를 보내시는 동안 먼저 건너편 벳새다로 가게 하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 곧바로 제자들을 재촉하여 배에 태워 먼저 건너편 벳새다로 가게 하시고, 그동안 무리를 돌려보내셨다.
ko.R: 그 일이 있은 뒤에 예수께서는 바로 제자들에게 배를 타고 먼저 호수 건너편 벳새다 마을로 가라고 하셨다. 예수께서는 남아서 사람들을 집으로 돌려보내셨다.

es.L: Y enseguida obligó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos a subir a la barca y a ir delante al otro lado, a Betsaida, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} despide a la multitud.
es.B: Enseguida Jesús insistió en que {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos subieran a la barca y cruzaran antes que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Betsaida, en la otra orilla, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} despedía a la multitud.
es.R: Enseguida Jesús les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que subieran a la barca y fueran antes que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} al otro lado del lago, al pueblo de Betsaida. Él se quedó para despedir a la gente.

fr.L: Et aussitôt {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} obligea {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples à monter dans la barque et à prendre les devants vers l’autre rive, vers Bethsaïda, tandis que {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} renvoie la foule.
fr.B: Aussitôt après, Jésus pressa {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de monter dans la barque et de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} précéder sur l’autre rive, à Bethsaïda, pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} renverrait la foule.
fr.R: Juste après, Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de monter dans la barque et de traverser le lac avant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour aller à la ville de Bethsaïda. Lui, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est resté pour renvoyer les gens chez eux.

sw.L: Na mara moja akawalazimisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kupanda mashuani na kutangulia kwenda ng'ambo, mpaka Bethsaida, wakati {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} anauaga umati.
sw.B: Mara moja Yesu aliwahimiza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wapande mashua na kumtangulia kwenda Bethsaida, ng'ambo ya pili, wakati {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akiuaga umati.
sw.R: Mara baada ya hayo, Yesu aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wapande mashua na kumtangulia kuvuka ziwa mpaka mji wa Bethsaida. Yeye alibaki nyuma ili awaage watu waende nyumbani.

decisions.choice: compelled: urged strongly, made them go
decisions.reason: The verb means to force or press. Mark does not say why. John 6:15 tells that the crowd wanted to make Jesus king.

decisions.choice: Bethsaida: a town on the north shore, east of where the Jordan enters the lake
alternatives: a town on the west shore
decisions.reason: The boat in fact lands at Gennesaret, on the west shore (6:53). The wind may have turned them back (6:48). Bethsaida is reached in 8:22.

decisions.choice: dismisses: a present tense, while he sends the crowd away
decisions.reason: He stays to send the crowd home while the disciples go.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says that Bethsaida was a town.

decisions.choice: "재촉하다" (L, B) for compelled; "벳새다"
decisions.reason: The verb means he urged them strongly (meaning decision); "재촉하다" says that without force. "벳새다" is the Protestant form (style guide, section 5).

decisions.choice: renvoie (L)
decisions.reason: Mark’s present tense (meaning decision m3) is kept at Literal, as the English does; Balanced and Readable put it in the past.

source.text: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken leave of them he departed to the mountain to pray.

en.L: And after taking leave of them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away to the mountain to pray.
en.B: After saying goodbye to them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went off up the mountain to pray.
en.R: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said goodbye to the people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up into the hills to pray.

vi.L: Và sau khi từ biệt họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi lên núi để cầu nguyện.
vi.B: Sau khi chào từ biệt họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên núi cầu nguyện.
vi.R: Sau khi chào tạm biệt dân chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi lên vùng đồi để cầu nguyện.

ko.L: 그리고 그들과 작별하신 후에 기도하시려고 산으로 떠나가셨다.
ko.B: 그들과 작별하신 뒤에, 기도하시려고 산으로 올라가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 사람들과 작별하시고 기도하시려고 산으로 올라가셨다.

es.L: Y después de despedirse de ellos, se fue al monte a orar.
es.B: Después de despedirse de ellos, subió al monte a orar.
es.R: Después de despedirse de la gente, subió al monte para orar.

fr.L: Et ayant pris congé d’eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en alla sur la montagne pour prier.
fr.B: Après leur avoir dit au revoir, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partit dans la montagne pour prier.
fr.R: Après avoir dit au revoir aux gens, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est monté dans les collines pour prier.

sw.L: Naye akiisha kuagana nao, akaenda zake mlimani kuomba.
sw.B: Baada ya kuwaaga, alikwenda mlimani kuomba.
sw.R: Baada ya kuwaaga watu, Yesu alipanda vilimani kuomba.

decisions.choice: them: the crowd, most likely
decisions.reason: The last group mentioned is the crowd. The disciples had already left (6:45).

decisions.choice: to pray: Jesus prays alone at turning points
decisions.reason: Mark shows him praying alone at 1:35 and in Gethsemane (14:32-39).

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hills above the lake
decisions.reason: The word can mean the hill country.

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, following the meaning note.

decisions.choice: el monte
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John (6:3, 6:15): "monte" covers the hill country above the lake (meaning decision), so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: la montagne (L, B); les collines (R)
decisions.reason: As in the French John 6:3 and 6:15: "dans la montagne" is the usual French for the hill country, without naming a peak (meaning decision m3); Readable says "les collines".

source.text: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And evening having come, was the boat in [the] middle of the sea, and he alone on the land.

en.L: And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [was] alone on the land.
en.B: When evening came, the boat was far out on the lake, and Jesus was alone on land.
en.R: When it was evening, the boat was out in the middle of Lake Galilee. Jesus was alone on the shore.

vi.L: Và khi chiều tối đến, chiếc thuyền ở giữa biển, và một mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở trên đất liền.
vi.B: Chiều tối đến, chiếc thuyền đã ra xa giữa biển, còn Đức Giê-xu ở một mình trên bờ.
vi.R: Khi trời tối, chiếc thuyền đang ở giữa hồ Ga-li-lê. Đức Giê-xu ở một mình trên bờ.

ko.L: 그리고 저녁이 되었을 때, 배는 바다 한가운데 있었고, 그분은 혼자 뭍에 계셨다.
ko.B: 저녁이 되었을 때, 배는 바다 한가운데 나가 있었고, 예수께서는 홀로 뭍에 계셨다.
ko.R: 저녁이 되었다. 그때 배는 갈릴리 호수 한가운데에 있었다. 예수께서는 혼자 호숫가에 계셨다.

es.L: Y al llegar la noche, la barca estaba en medio del mar, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} solo en tierra.
es.B: Al anochecer, la barca estaba lejos de la orilla, en medio del mar, y Jesús estaba solo en tierra.
es.R: Cuando llegó la noche, la barca estaba en medio del lago de Galilea. Jesús estaba solo en la orilla.

fr.L: Et le soir venu, la barque était au milieu de la mer, et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} [était] seul à terre.
fr.B: Le soir venu, la barque était au milieu de la mer, et Jésus était seul à terre.
fr.R: Quand le soir est arrivé, la barque était au milieu du lac de Galilée. Jésus était seul sur le rivage.

sw.L: Na jioni ilipofika, mashua ilikuwa katikati ya bahari, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} [alikuwa] peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} nchi kavu.
sw.B: Jioni ilipofika, mashua ilikuwa mbali katikati ya bahari, na Yesu alikuwa peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} nchi kavu.
sw.R: Ilipofika jioni, mashua ilikuwa katikati ya Ziwa Galilaya. Yesu alikuwa peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ufuoni.

decisions.choice: evening: after sunset, the start of the night
decisions.reason: The meal took place late in the day (6:35); now night has come.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the sea: far from land
decisions.reason: The phrase means well out on the water.

decisions.choice: the lake (B); Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: As in chapters 1 to 5.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L, B); "hồ Ga-li-lê", "hồ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Gospel calls the Lake of Galilee a "sea". As in Mark 5 and the Vietnamese John, Literal and Balanced keep "biển" and Readable says "hồ" (lake); used through 6:47-53.

decisions.choice: el mar (L, B); el lago (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "mar", the Greek word and the name Spanish readers know (as in 1:16); Readable says "lago", since the Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: la mer (L, B); le lac (R)
alternatives: le lac (B), as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: As in the French of John (6:16) and of Mark 3-5: Literal and Balanced keep "la mer", the Greek word and the usual French name; Readable says "le lac" so young readers do not picture the open sea. The same in 6:48-49.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν, ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς, περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης· καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen them straining in the rowing, was for the wind against them, about [the] fourth watch of the night he comes to them walking on the sea; and he was wanting to pass by them.

en.L: And seeing them straining in the rowing, for the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to them, walking on the sea; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted to pass by them.
en.B: He saw them struggling at the oars, since the wind was against them. Toward the end of the night, in the fourth watch, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came out to them walking on the lake. He meant to pass by them.
en.R: Jesus saw that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were working very hard to row the boat, because the wind was blowing against them. Sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning, Jesus came to them. He was walking on top of the water! He was going to go on past them.

vi.L: Và thấy họ khổ sở chèo chống, vì gió ngược với họ, khoảng canh thứ tư của đêm, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt biển đến với họ; và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn đi ngang qua họ.
vi.B: Ngài thấy họ chèo chống vất vả vì gió ngược. Gần sáng, vào khoảng canh thứ tư, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt biển đến với họ. Ngài định đi ngang qua họ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thấy các môn đồ chèo thuyền rất vất vả, vì gió thổi ngược. Vào khoảng từ ba đến sáu giờ sáng, Đức Giê-xu đến với họ. Ngài đi bộ trên mặt nước! Ngài định đi ngang qua họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들이 노를 젓느라 시달리는 것을 보시고, 바람이 그들에게 마주 불어왔기 때문인데, 밤 넷째 경쯤에 바다 위를 걸으시며 그들에게 오신다. 그리고 그들을 지나쳐 가려고 하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 맞바람 때문에 제자들이 노를 젓느라 몹시 애쓰는 것을 보셨다. 밤이 거의 끝나 갈 무렵, 밤 넷째 경에 예수께서 바다 위를 걸어서 그들에게 오셨다. 예수께서는 그들 곁을 지나가려고 하셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 제자들이 노를 젓느라 몹시 힘들어하는 것을 보셨다. 바람이 그들 쪽으로 마주 불고 있었기 때문이다. 새벽 세 시에서 여섯 시 사이에 예수께서 그들에게 오셨다. 예수께서는 물 위를 걷고 계셨다! 예수께서는 그들 곁을 지나가려고 하셨다.

es.L: Y viéndolos fatigados al remar, porque el viento les era contrario, hacia la cuarta vigilia de la noche viene hacia ellos caminando sobre el mar; y quería pasar junto a ellos.
es.B: Vio que se esforzaban remando, porque tenían el viento en contra. Hacia el final de la noche, en la cuarta vigilia, fue hacia ellos caminando sobre el mar. Quería pasar junto a ellos.
es.R: Jesús vio que a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos les costaba mucho remar, porque el viento soplaba en contra. Entre las tres y las seis de la mañana, Jesús fue hacia ellos. ¡Iba caminando sobre el agua! Iba a pasar junto a ellos.

fr.L: Et les voyant s’épuiser à ramer, car le vent leur était contraire, vers la quatrième veille de la nuit {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient vers eux, marchant sur la mer ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait passer à côté d’eux.
fr.B: Il les vit peiner à ramer, car le vent leur était contraire. Vers la fin de la nuit, à la quatrième veille, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint vers eux en marchant sur la mer. Il voulait passer près d’eux.
fr.R: Jésus a vu que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples avaient beaucoup de mal à faire avancer la barque, parce que le vent soufflait contre eux. Entre trois heures et six heures du matin, Jésus est venu vers eux. Il marchait sur l’eau ! Il allait passer à côté d’eux.

sw.L: Na alipowaona wakihangaika katika kupiga makasia, kwa maana upepo ulikuwa kinyume chao, karibu na zamu ya nne ya usiku anakuja kwao akitembea juu ya bahari; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alitaka kuwapita.
sw.B: Aliwaona wakihangaika kupiga makasia, kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa ukivuma kinyume chao. Karibu na mwisho wa usiku, katika zamu ya nne, akawaendea akitembea juu ya bahari. Alikusudia kuwapita.
sw.R: Yesu aliona kwamba wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakijitahidi sana kupiga makasia, kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa ukivuma kinyume chao. Kati ya saa tisa usiku na saa kumi na mbili alfajiri, Yesu aliwaendea. Alikuwa akitembea juu ya maji! Alikuwa anataka kuwapita.

decisions.choice: the fourth watch of the night: from about three to six in the morning
decisions.reason: The Romans divided the night into four watches. The disciples have rowed most of the night.

decisions.choice: he wanted to pass by them: as God passed by Moses and Elijah to show himself
alternatives: he meant to walk ahead of them
decisions.reason: God passed by Moses to show his glory (Exodus 33:19-22; 34:6) and passed by Elijah on the mountain (1 Kings 19:11). The words most likely mean Jesus meant to show himself to them, not to leave them. Some read it simply as walking past.

decisions.choice: walking on the sea: what scripture says God alone does
decisions.reason: Job 9:8 says God alone treads on the waves of the sea (see Psalm 77:20).

decisions.choice: straining: tormented, struggling hard
decisions.reason: The word means to be tormented; here, worn out by rowing against the wind.

decisions.choice: toward the end of the night, in the fourth watch (B); sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning (R)
alternatives: about the fourth watch of the night
decisions.reason: Balanced shows where the watch falls in the night; Readable gives the time in modern terms.

decisions.choice: "canh thứ tư" (L, B), with "gần sáng" (B); "từ ba đến sáu giờ sáng" (R)
decisions.reason: The Romans divided the night into four watches, and the fourth ran from about three to six in the morning (meaning decision). The traditional Vietnamese night has five "canh", and "canh tư" means about one to three, so the drafts write "canh thứ tư" and Balanced adds "gần sáng" to avoid that reading.

decisions.choice: "밤 넷째 경" (L, B); "새벽 세 시에서 여섯 시 사이" (R)
decisions.reason: "사경" is the fourth of the five watches of the traditional Korean night and would give the wrong hour; "밤 넷째 경" keeps the Roman count of four watches, and Readable gives the modern time (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: pasar junto a ellos
decisions.reason: "Pasar de largo" would say he meant to ignore them. "Pasar junto a" keeps the plain verb, which recalls God passing by Moses and Elijah (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: passer à côté d’eux (L, R); passer près d’eux (B)
decisions.reason: French "dépasser" would mean to overtake them in a race; "passer près d’eux" keeps the picture of God passing by Moses and Elijah to show himself (meaning decision m2, with its footnote).

decisions.choice: kati ya saa tisa usiku na saa kumi na mbili alfajiri
alternatives: kati ya saa tisa na saa kumi na mbili
decisions.reason: The fourth watch ran from about three to six in the morning. Swahili time counts the hours from six o'clock, so that is "saa tisa usiku" to "saa kumi na mbili alfajiri"; the words "usiku" (night) and "alfajiri" (dawn) make the time plain to every reader.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἔδοξαν ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀνέκραξαν, πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen him on the sea walking they thought that a ghost it is, and cried out; \v 50 all for him saw and were troubled.

en.L: But when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the sea, they thought that it was a ghost, and they cried out, \v 50 for they all saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were terrified.
en.B: When they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the lake, they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a ghost and cried out in fear, \v 50 for every one of them saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and they were shaken.
en.R: The followers saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the water. They thought {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was a ghost, and they screamed. \v 50 All of them saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were very frightened.

vi.L: Nhưng khi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt biển, họ tưởng là ma và kêu thét lên, \v 50 vì tất cả đều thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đều hoảng sợ.
vi.B: Khi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt biển, họ tưởng là ma nên kêu thét lên, \v 50 vì tất cả đều thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đều kinh hoảng.
vi.R: Các môn đồ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt nước. Họ tưởng là ma nên la hét lên. \v 50 Tất cả đều thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ rất sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 그분이 바다 위를 걸으시는 것을 보고 유령이라고 생각하여 소리를 질렀다. \v 50 모두가 그분을 보고 겁에 질렸기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들은 예수께서 바다 위를 걸어오시는 것을 보고 유령인 줄 알고 비명을 질렀다. \v 50 그들이 모두 예수를 보고 겁에 질렸기 때문이다.
ko.R: 제자들은 예수께서 물 위를 걸어오시는 것을 보았다. 그들은 유령인 줄 알고 비명을 질렀다. \v 50 모두가 예수를 보고 몹시 무서워했다.

es.L: Pero ellos, al verlo caminando sobre el mar, pensaron que era un fantasma, y gritaron; \v 50 porque todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron y se turbaron.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron caminando sobre el mar, creyeron que era un fantasma y se pusieron a gritar de miedo, \v 50 porque todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron y quedaron espantados.
es.R: Los discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron caminando sobre el agua. Pensaron que era un fantasma, y gritaron. \v 50 Todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron, y tenían mucho miedo.

fr.L: Mais eux, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyant marcher sur la mer, pensèrent que c’était un fantôme et poussèrent des cris, \v 50 car tous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} virent et furent troublés.
fr.B: En {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyant marcher sur la mer, ils crurent que c’était un fantôme et poussèrent des cris d’effroi, \v 50 car tous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient vu et ils étaient bouleversés.
fr.R: Les disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont vu marcher sur l’eau. Ils ont cru que c’était un fantôme, et ils se sont mis à hurler. \v 50 Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient tous vu, et ils avaient très peur.

sw.L: Lakini wao walipomwona akitembea juu ya bahari, walidhani kwamba ni mzimu, wakapiga kelele, \v 50 kwa maana wote walimwona, wakafadhaika.
sw.B: Walipomwona akitembea juu ya bahari, walidhani ni mzimu, wakapiga yowe kwa hofu, \v 50 kwa sababu wote walimwona, wakatetemeka.
sw.R: Wanafunzi walimwona akitembea juu ya maji. Wakadhani ni mzimu, wakapiga kelele. \v 50 Wote walimwona, nao wakaogopa sana.

decisions.choice: ghost: an apparition, a phantom
decisions.reason: The word means something that appears but is not real.

decisions.choice: for they all saw him: it was not one man's imagination
decisions.reason: Mark explains why they all cried out.

decisions.choice: terrified: shaken, thrown into fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to be stirred up or deeply disturbed.

decisions.choice: mzimu
decisions.reason: "Mzimu" is an apparition or ghost. "Pepo" is kept for the demons of 5:15 and 6:13, and "kivuli" (shadow) is less clear to a modern reader.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εὐθὺς ἐλάλησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

records.literal_gloss: But he immediately spoke with them, and says to them, Take courage, I am, do not fear.

en.L: But immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke with them and says to them, "Take courage; I am [he]; do not be afraid."
en.B: But right away {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them. "Be brave," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "It is I. Stop being afraid."
en.R: Right away Jesus spoke to them. "Cheer up!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "It is I, Jesus. Do not be afraid."

vi.L: Nhưng lập tức {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói chuyện với họ, và nói với họ: "Hãy vững lòng! Ta đây; đừng sợ."
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} liền nói với họ: "Hãy can đảm lên! Ta đây. Đừng sợ nữa."
vi.R: Ngay lập tức, Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy yên tâm! Chính Ta đây! Đừng sợ!"

ko.L: 그러나 그분은 곧 그들과 이야기하시며 그들에게 말씀하신다. "용기를 내어라. 나다. 두려워하지 마라."
ko.B: 그러자 예수께서 곧바로 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "용기를 내어라. 나다. 이제 두려워하지 마라."
ko.R: 예수께서 바로 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "힘을 내라! 나다, 예수다. 무서워하지 마라."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} enseguida habló con ellos, y les dice: «¡Ánimo! Yo soy; no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les habló enseguida. «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} ánimo», les dijo. «Soy yo. {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} de tener miedo».
es.R: Enseguida Jesús les habló: «¡Ánimo! Soy yo, Jesús. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo».

fr.L: Mais aussitôt {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parla avec eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Courage ! Je suis, [c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}] ; n’ayez pas peur. »
fr.B: Mais aussitôt {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur parla : « Courage, dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Cessez d’avoir peur. »
fr.R: Tout de suite, Jésus leur a parlé : « Courage ! leur a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit. C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, Jésus. N’ayez pas peur. »

sw.L: Lakini mara moja alisema nao, na anawaambia, "Jipeni moyo; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye; msiogope."
sw.B: Lakini mara moja aliongea nao. Akasema, "Jipeni moyo! Ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Acheni kuogopa."
sw.R: Mara hiyo Yesu akasema nao, "Changamkeni! Ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, Yesu. Msiogope."

decisions.choice: I am: he tells them who he is, in words that echo the name God gave himself
alternatives: only: it is me, a simple greeting
decisions.reason: In ordinary speech the words mean "it is I". But God spoke of himself as "I am" (Exodus 3:14), and in Isaiah God says "I am he" and tells his people not to fear (Isaiah 43:10; 51:12). Coming from one who walks on the sea, the words most likely carry both senses. Jesus uses them again in 14:62.

decisions.choice: take courage: be brave, do not lose heart
decisions.reason: The verb means to be confident or bold.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: stop being afraid
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" usually tells someone to stop what they are already doing.

decisions.choice: It is I, Jesus.
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name so that the plain sense is clear. The meaning note gives the deeper sense.

decisions.choice: "Ta đây" (L, B); "Chính Ta đây" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese John (6:20): "Ta là" with nothing after it is not a sentence in Vietnamese, so even Literal says "Ta đây" (it is I), the plain sense; the echo of God's name is left to the meaning decision and its footnote. Readable makes it emphatic with "chính" rather than adding the name, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "나다" for "I am" at every level; "용기를 내어라" (L, B), "힘을 내라" (R) for take courage
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John 6:20, "나다" is plain Korean for "it is I" and leaves room for the echo of God's name noted in the meaning decision. "안심하여라" says "be at ease"; "용기를 내어라" keeps the call to courage.

decisions.choice: Yo soy (L); Soy yo (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John 6:20: "Soy yo" is the plain Spanish for "it is me", the sense to frightened men in a boat. Literal keeps "Yo soy", still a complete answer in Spanish, which keeps the echo of God's own words (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Je suis, [c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}] (L); c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the French John 6:20: French says "c’est moi" where English says "it is I". Literal keeps the bare "Je suis", which carries the echo of God’s name noted in meaning decision m1 (with its footnote), and brackets the plain sense; Balanced and Readable give the plain sense. "Moi" for Jesus takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: mimi ndiye (L); Ni mimi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Swahili of John 6:20: "mimi ndiye" (I am the one, I am he) keeps the shape of the Greek "I am", with the echo of God's name the meaning note mentions; Balanced and Readable say "Ni mimi" (it is I), what anyone would call out in the dark.

source.text: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.

records.literal_gloss: And he went up to them into the boat, and ceased the wind.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat beside them, and the wind dropped.
en.R: Jesus climbed into their boat. The wind stopped.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên thuyền với họ, và gió ngừng lại.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bước lên thuyền với họ, và gió lặng đi.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu leo lên thuyền với họ. Gió ngừng thổi.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게로 배에 오르시자, 바람이 그쳤다.
ko.B: 그리고 예수께서 그들이 탄 배에 오르시자, 바람이 잠잠해졌다.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들의 배에 올라타셨다. 그러자 바람이 멈추었다.

es.L: Y subió adonde estaban ellos, a la barca, y el viento cesó.
es.B: Luego subió a la barca con ellos, y el viento se calmó.
es.R: Jesús subió a la barca con ellos. Entonces el viento dejó de soplar.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta vers eux dans la barque, et le vent tomba.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans la barque auprès d’eux, et le vent s’apaisa.
fr.R: Jésus est monté dans leur barque, et le vent s’est arrêté.

sw.L: Naye akapanda kwao mashuani, na upepo ukakoma.
sw.B: Kisha akaingia mashuani pamoja nao, na upepo ukatulia.
sw.R: Yesu akapanda ndani ya mashua yao. Upepo ukakoma.

decisions.choice: ceased: grew tired, died down
decisions.reason: The same verb as at 4:39.

decisions.choice: the wind stops when he comes into the boat
decisions.reason: As in 4:39, the storm obeys him.

source.text: καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐξίσταντο, οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις, ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη.

records.literal_gloss: And exceedingly out of measure in themselves they were amazed, \v 52 not for they understood about the loaves, but was of them the heart hardened.

en.L: And they were utterly astonished within themselves, \v 52 for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart had been hardened.
en.B: They were beside themselves with amazement, \v 52 for they had not grasped what the loaves showed. Their hearts had been hardened.
en.R: The followers were completely amazed. \v 52 They had not understood what the miracle of the loaves meant. Their hearts were hard, and they could not understand.

vi.L: Và họ vô cùng kinh ngạc trong lòng, \v 52 vì họ đã không hiểu về [việc] những cái bánh, nhưng lòng họ đã bị chai cứng.
vi.B: Họ hết sức sửng sốt, \v 52 vì họ chưa hiểu được ý nghĩa của việc những cái bánh. Lòng họ đã bị chai cứng.
vi.R: Các môn đồ vô cùng kinh ngạc. \v 52 Họ chưa hiểu phép lạ về những cái bánh có ý nghĩa gì. Lòng họ cứng cỏi nên họ không thể hiểu.

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 속으로 너무나도 몹시 놀랐다. \v 52 그들이 빵에 관하여 깨닫지 못하고, 오히려 그들의 마음이 굳어져 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 제자들은 너무 놀라 어찌할 바를 몰랐다. \v 52 빵의 일이 무엇을 보여 주는지 깨닫지 못했기 때문이다. 그들의 마음이 굳어져 있었다.
ko.R: 제자들은 몹시 놀랐다. \v 52 그들은 예수께서 빵을 먹이신 일이 무엇을 뜻하는지 깨닫지 못했다. 그들의 마음이 굳어서 깨달을 수 없었던 것이다.

es.L: Y se asombraban en extremo dentro de sí mismos, \v 52 porque no habían entendido lo de los panes, sino que su corazón estaba endurecido.
es.B: Estaban completamente fuera de sí por el asombro, \v 52 porque no habían comprendido lo que significaban los panes. Tenían el corazón endurecido.
es.R: Los discípulos estaban muy asombrados. \v 52 No habían entendido lo que significaba el milagro de los panes. Tenían el corazón endurecido, y no podían entender.

fr.L: Et ils étaient en eux-mêmes extrêmement stupéfaits, \v 52 car ils n’avaient pas compris au sujet des pains, mais leur cœur avait été endurci.
fr.B: Ils étaient complètement bouleversés, \v 52 car ils n’avaient pas compris ce que signifiaient les pains : leur cœur était endurci.
fr.R: Les disciples étaient complètement stupéfaits. \v 52 Ils n’avaient pas compris ce que voulait dire le miracle des pains. Leur cœur était fermé, et ils ne pouvaient pas comprendre.

sw.L: Nao wakashangaa mno kupita kiasi ndani yao wenyewe, \v 52 kwa maana hawakuwa wameelewa habari za mikate, bali mioyo yao ilikuwa imefanywa migumu.
sw.B: Wakastaajabu kupita kiasi, \v 52 kwa sababu hawakuwa wameelewa maana ya ile mikate. Mioyo yao ilikuwa imeshupazwa.
sw.R: Wanafunzi walishangaa sana. \v 52 Hawakuwa wameelewa maana ya muujiza ule wa mikate. Mioyo yao ilikuwa migumu, na hawakuweza kuelewa.

decisions.choice: understood about the loaves: what the feeding showed about who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Had they understood the feeding, they would not be so astonished that he walks on the sea.

decisions.choice: heart hardened: a mind dull and closed
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought. The same kind of hardness was said of Jesus' opponents in 3:5; now it is said of the disciples (8:17).

decisions.choice: had been hardened: a passive that does not say who hardened them
decisions.reason: Mark states their condition and leaves the cause unnamed.

decisions.choice: they were amazed, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and they marveled". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and they could not understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what a hard heart means here, as at 3:5.

decisions.choice: "마음이 굳어지다" at every level
decisions.reason: The same picture as the Korean Mark 3:5 ("마음이 굳어 있는 것"); the passive does not say who hardened them (meaning decision), and Korean "굳어지다" leaves that open too.

decisions.choice: avait été endurci (L); était endurci (B)
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who hardened their hearts (meaning decision m3). French "s’était endurci" would make them the agents, so Literal keeps the passive and Balanced the plain state.

source.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having crossed over to the land they came to Gennesaret and anchored.

en.L: And when they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and anchored.
en.B: When they had crossed the lake, they came ashore at Gennesaret and tied up the boat.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed the lake and came to land near the town of Gennesaret. They tied the boat up there.

vi.L: Và sau khi đã qua đến đất liền, họ đến Ghê-nê-xa-rét và cập bến.
vi.B: Khi đã qua bên kia biển, họ đến vùng Ghê-nê-xa-rét và buộc thuyền vào bờ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ qua bên kia hồ và đến vùng Ghê-nê-xa-rét. Họ buộc thuyền lại ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 건너가서 게네사렛 땅에 이르러 배를 댔다.
ko.B: 그들은 바다를 건너 게네사렛에 이르러 배를 댔다.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들과 함께 호수를 건너 게네사렛 근처에 이르셨다. 그들은 그곳에 배를 매어 두었다.

es.L: Y habiendo cruzado, llegaron a tierra en Genesaret y atracaron.
es.B: Cuando terminaron de cruzar el mar, llegaron a tierra en Genesaret y amarraron la barca.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos cruzaron el lago y llegaron a la orilla cerca de Genesaret. Allí amarraron la barca.

fr.L: Et ayant traversé jusqu’à la terre, ils vinrent à Génésareth et accostèrent.
fr.B: Après la traversée, ils touchèrent terre à Génésareth et y amarrèrent la barque.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont traversé le lac et sont arrivés dans la plaine de Génésareth. Ils ont attaché la barque là.

sw.L: Nao walipokwisha kuvuka, wakafika nchi kavu huko Genesareti, wakatia nanga.
sw.B: Walipokwisha kuvuka ziwa, walifika pwani huko Genesareti, wakaifunga mashua.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walivuka ziwa, wakafika nchi kavu huko Genesareti. Wakaifunga mashua yao pale.

decisions.choice: Gennesaret: a fertile plain on the west shore, south of Capernaum
decisions.reason: The lake was also called the Lake of Gennesaret (Luke 5:1).

decisions.choice: they came to Gennesaret, not to Bethsaida (6:45)
decisions.reason: Mark does not say why they landed elsewhere. The wind may have driven them off course.

decisions.choice: anchored: drew in to shore and moored
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring a boat into harbor.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who crossed.

decisions.choice: "vùng Ghê-nê-xa-rét"
decisions.reason: Gennesaret is a plain on the western shore (meaning decision), so Vietnamese says "vùng" (region) rather than "thị trấn" (town), which the English Readable has.

decisions.choice: "게네사렛"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant form (style guide, section 5).

decisions.choice: cerca de Genesaret
decisions.reason: Gennesaret was a plain on the shore (meaning decision), so Readable does not call it a town.

decisions.choice: la plaine de Génésareth (R)
alternatives: la ville de Génésareth, as the English Readable
decisions.reason: Gennesaret was a fertile plain on the west shore (meaning decision m1), so Readable says "la plaine" rather than calling it a town.

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: And having come out they out of the boat, immediately having recognized him \v 55 they ran around all the region that and began on the mats those sick to carry around, wherever they were hearing that he is.

en.L: And when they came out of the boat, immediately [people] recognized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \v 55 and ran around that whole region and began to carry around on mats those who were sick, to wherever they heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.
en.B: As soon as they stepped out of the boat, people knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. \v 55 They ran all through that region and began bringing those who were ill on their mats to any place where they heard {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.
en.R: The moment they stepped out of the boat, the people there knew it was Jesus. \v 55 They ran all over that area to tell others. Then they carried sick people on mats to any place where they heard Jesus was.

vi.L: Và khi họ ra khỏi thuyền, lập tức [người ta] nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} \v 55 và chạy khắp cả vùng ấy, và bắt đầu khiêng những người đau ốm trên cáng đến bất cứ nơi nào họ nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở.
vi.B: Họ vừa ra khỏi thuyền thì người ta nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay. \v 55 Họ chạy khắp vùng ấy và bắt đầu khiêng những người bệnh trên cáng đến bất cứ nơi nào nghe nói {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang có mặt.
vi.R: Vừa khi họ ra khỏi thuyền, dân ở đó nhận ra ngay đó là Đức Giê-xu. \v 55 Họ chạy khắp vùng ấy để báo cho người khác biết. Rồi họ khiêng người bệnh trên cáng đến bất cứ nơi nào họ nghe Đức Giê-xu đang ở.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 배에서 나오자, 곧 [사람들이] 그분을 알아보고 \v 55 그 온 지방을 두루 뛰어다니며, 그분이 계신다는 소문을 듣는 곳마다 병든 사람들을 들것에 실어 나르기 시작했다.
ko.B: 그들이 배에서 내리자마자 사람들이 예수를 알아보았다. \v 55 그들은 그 온 지방을 뛰어다니며, 예수께서 계시다는 소문이 들리는 곳이면 어디든지 병든 사람들을 들것에 실어 날라 오기 시작했다.
ko.R: 예수께서 배에서 내리시자, 그곳 사람들이 바로 예수를 알아보았다. \v 55 그들은 그 지방 곳곳을 뛰어다니며 다른 사람들에게 알렸다. 그리고 예수께서 계시다는 곳이면 어디든지 아픈 사람들을 들것에 실어 데려왔다.

es.L: Y cuando ellos salieron de la barca, enseguida {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} reconocieron, \v 55 y recorrieron corriendo toda aquella región, y comenzaron a llevar en camillas a los que estaban enfermos adonde oían que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba.
es.B: En cuanto bajaron de la barca, la gente reconoció a Jesús. \v 55 Recorrieron toda aquella región y comenzaron a llevar a los enfermos en sus camillas a cualquier lugar donde oían que estaba.
es.R: Apenas bajaron de la barca, la gente de allí reconoció a Jesús. \v 55 Corrieron por toda aquella región para avisar a los demás. Luego llevaban a los enfermos en camillas a cualquier lugar donde oían que estaba Jesús.

fr.L: Et comme ils sortaient de la barque, aussitôt [les gens] {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnurent \v 55 et parcoururent en courant toute cette région, et commencèrent à transporter sur des nattes ceux qui étaient malades, là où ils entendaient dire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était.
fr.B: Dès qu’ils furent descendus de la barque, les gens reconnurent Jésus. \v 55 Ils parcoururent toute la région en courant et se mirent à apporter les malades sur leurs nattes partout où ils entendaient dire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se trouvait.
fr.R: Dès qu’ils sont descendus de la barque, les gens de l’endroit ont reconnu Jésus. \v 55 Ils ont couru partout dans la région pour prévenir les autres. Puis ils ont transporté des malades sur des nattes jusqu’à l’endroit où ils entendaient dire que Jésus était.

sw.L: Na walipotoka mashuani, mara moja [watu] wakamtambua, \v 55 wakazunguka mbio nchi ile yote, wakaanza kuwabeba juu ya mikeka wale waliokuwa wagonjwa, [wakiwapeleka] popote waliposikia kwamba yupo.
sw.B: Mara tu walipotoka mashuani, watu walimtambua. \v 55 Wakakimbia kila mahali katika eneo lile lote, wakaanza kuwabeba wagonjwa juu ya mikeka yao na kuwapeleka popote waliposikia kwamba yupo.
sw.R: Mara tu walipotoka kwenye mashua, watu wa huko walimtambua Yesu. \v 55 Wakakimbia kila mahali katika eneo lile kuwaambia wengine. Kisha wakawabeba wagonjwa juu ya mikeka, wakawapeleka mahali popote waliposikia kwamba Yesu yupo.

decisions.choice: mats: pallets, the poor man's bed
decisions.reason: The same word as at 2:4, 2:11.

decisions.choice: wherever they heard he was: they kept following news of him
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows people following reports of where Jesus was from day to day.

decisions.choice: recognized him: the people of that region
decisions.reason: The participle has no stated subject. The verbs that follow show it is the people there.

decisions.choice: to tell others
decisions.reason: Readable says why they ran about, which the carrying of the sick implies.

decisions.choice: "cáng"
decisions.reason: The word is a pallet, the poor man's bed (meaning decision). Here the sick are carried on it, and "cáng" (stretcher) says that plainly; "giường" would suggest a heavy bed.

decisions.choice: "들것" for krabattos
decisions.reason: A pallet the sick were carried on (meaning decision); "침상" is the older word and suggests a bed frame, while "들것" says how they were brought.

decisions.choice: lo reconocieron, with no supplied [people]
decisions.reason: The Spanish verb shows its plural subject, so Literal needs none of the English brackets here.

decisions.choice: nattes
decisions.reason: A mat or pallet, the poor man’s bed (meaning decision m1); "natte" is the word the French John uses for the same object (5:8-11). "Grabat" is traditional but little known.

decisions.choice: mikeka
decisions.reason: "Mkeka", the woven mat a poor person sleeps on, is the picture the Greek word gives; "godoro" (mattress) and "kitanda" (bed) are too grand.

source.text: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο.

records.literal_gloss: And wherever he was entering into villages or into towns or into countryside, in the marketplaces they were laying the sick, and were begging him that if only the fringe of the cloak of him they might touch; and as many as touched him were being saved.

en.L: And wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, into villages or into towns or into the countryside, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that they might touch even the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak; and as many as touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were made well.
en.B: Wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, whether villages or towns or farms, people set their sick down in the marketplaces and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to let them touch just the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak. Everyone who touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was made well.
en.R: Jesus went into villages, towns, and farm areas. Wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, people brought their sick friends to the marketplaces. They begged Jesus to let the sick people touch just the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak. And everyone who touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was healed.

vi.L: Và bất cứ nơi nào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi vào, làng mạc, thành thị hay thôn quê, người ta đặt những người bệnh tại các nơi họp chợ, và nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ chạm được dù chỉ là viền áo choàng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; và hễ ai chạm đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều được lành.
vi.B: Bất cứ nơi nào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, dù là làng mạc, thành thị hay thôn quê, người ta cũng đem người bệnh đặt ở các khu chợ, và nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ chỉ được chạm vào viền áo choàng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thôi. Ai chạm vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng đều được lành.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đi vào các làng mạc, thành thị và vùng quê. Ngài đi đến đâu, người ta cũng đem người bệnh đến các khu chợ. Họ nài xin Đức Giê-xu cho những người bệnh chỉ cần được chạm vào viền áo choàng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Và ai chạm vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng đều được chữa lành.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 마을이든 고을이든 농촌이든 어디로 들어가시든지, [사람들이] 장터에 병자들을 눕혀 놓고, 그분의 겉옷 술만이라도 만지게 해 달라고 그분께 간청하고 있었다. 그리고 그분을 만진 사람은 모두 구원을 받았다.
ko.B: 마을이든 고을이든 농촌이든, 예수께서 들어가시는 곳마다 사람들은 병자들을 장터에 데려다 놓고, 예수의 겉옷 자락만이라도 만지게 해 달라고 간청했다. 그리고 예수를 만진 사람은 모두 나았다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 여러 마을과 고을과 농촌을 다니셨다. 예수께서 가시는 곳마다 사람들은 아픈 사람들을 장터로 데려왔다. 그리고 아픈 사람들이 예수의 옷자락 끝이라도 만지게 해 달라고 예수께 빌었다. 예수를 만진 사람은 모두 병이 나았다.

es.L: Y dondequiera que entraba, en aldeas o en ciudades o en campos, ponían a los enfermos en las plazas, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaban que [los dejara] tocar aunque fuera el borde de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto; y todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tocaban quedaban sanos.
es.B: Dondequiera que iba, fueran aldeas, pueblos o campos, la gente ponía a sus enfermos en las plazas y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaba que los dejara tocar siquiera el borde de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto. Y todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tocaban quedaban sanos.
es.R: Jesús iba a aldeas, pueblos y campos. Dondequiera que iba, la gente llevaba a sus amigos enfermos a las plazas. Le rogaban a Jesús que dejara a los enfermos tocar aunque fuera el borde de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto. Y todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tocaban quedaban sanos.

fr.L: Et partout où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entrait, dans des villages, dans des villes ou dans des campagnes, on déposait les malades sur les places, et on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliait de pouvoir toucher ne serait-ce que la frange de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau ; et tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} touchaient étaient sauvés.
fr.B: Partout où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait, dans les villages, les villes ou les fermes, on déposait les malades sur les places et on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliait de les laisser toucher ne serait-ce que la frange de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau. Et tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} touchaient étaient guéris.
fr.R: Jésus allait dans les villages, dans les villes et dans les fermes. Partout où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait, les gens apportaient leurs amis malades sur les places. Ils suppliaient Jésus de laisser les malades toucher seulement le bord de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau. Et tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} touchaient étaient guéris.

sw.L: Na popote alipoingia, katika vijiji au katika miji au mashambani, waliwaweka wagonjwa sokoni, wakawa wakimsihi kwamba waguse angalau upindo wa vazi {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}; na wote waliomgusa walikuwa wakipona.
sw.B: Kila alipoingia, iwe vijijini, mijini au mashambani, watu waliwaweka wagonjwa wao kwenye viwanja vya soko, wakamsihi awaruhusu waguse angalau upindo wa vazi {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. Kila aliyemgusa alipona.
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda vijijini, mijini na mashambani. Kila mahali alipokwenda, watu waliwaleta rafiki zao wagonjwa sokoni. Wakamsihi Yesu awaruhusu wagonjwa waguse angalau upindo wa vazi {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. Na kila aliyemgusa aliponywa.

decisions.choice: the fringe of his cloak: the edge, perhaps the tassels the law required
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels on the corners of their cloaks (Numbers 15:38-39; Deuteronomy 22:12). The word can mean those tassels or simply the edge.

decisions.choice: were made well: the verb also means were saved
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the woman healed in 5:28 and 5:34. Healing is a sign of God's saving work.

decisions.choice: they were laying, begging, being healed: it happened again and again
decisions.reason: The tenses describe what happened in place after place.

decisions.choice: marketplaces: open squares in towns and villages
decisions.reason: The open square was where people gathered.

decisions.choice: their sick friends; the sick people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear who was carried and who touched.

decisions.choice: "viền áo"
decisions.reason: The fringe is the edge of the cloak, perhaps the tassels the law required (meaning decision). "Viền áo" (edge) is the safe plain sense; "tua áo" would settle on the tassels.

decisions.choice: "겉옷 술" (L); "겉옷 자락" (B); "옷자락 끝" (R); "구원을 받다" (L), "낫다" (B, R) for sozo
decisions.reason: The fringe may be the tassels the law required (meaning decision), which Literal names; Balanced and Readable say the edge of the cloak. For the verb, Literal keeps "구원" as in the Korean Mark 5:23-34, since the verb also means "were saved".

decisions.choice: quedaban sanos
decisions.reason: The verb also means "were saved" (meaning decision); here, as in the English, every level gives the healing, which is the sense in the context.

decisions.choice: étaient sauvés (L); étaient guéris (B, R)
alternatives: étaient guéris (L), as the English Literal
decisions.reason: The verb means both "made well" and "saved" (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "sauvés", as French Literal does for the same verb in 5:23, 5:28 and 5:34, so the link stays visible; Balanced and Readable give the plain sense.
